Osun election: Ex-PDP guber aspirant endorses Adeleke
items.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo A former gubernatorial aspirant of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, in Osun State, Mr Adebayo Adedamola, popularly known as Fryo, has announced his endorsement of Governor Ademola Adeleke for the August 15, 2026 governorship election. Adedamola was nominated by a faction of the PDP for the August 15 poll. He polled 919 votes out of 957 cast in the primary held in Osogbo, the state capital. However, his name was not among the final list of candidates for the election announced by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Adedamola, alongside his supporters, said the decision followed extensive consultations, sober reflection and assessment of the political circumstances in the state. “I have arrived at this decision based on my assessment of the political circumstances in our state and my conviction that, at this particular moment, this is the direction I am prepared to support. “I encourage all PDP members, supporters and party structures across the state who believe in my leadership and judgment to support the emergence of His Excellency, Senator Ademola Adeleke, at the August 15 gubernatorial election,” Adedamola stated. The PDP chieftain said he remains proud of his participation in the party’s primary and expressed gratitude to those who supported his candidacy. He, however, stressed that politics is also about making difficult decisions at critical moments, adding, “Politics is not only about contesting elections. Politics is also about understanding the realities of the moment, making difficult decisions when necessary, and putting the larger interest of our people above personal ambition.” Adedamola noted that he had already communicated his position to PDP leaders, members and stakeholders across the state. Speaking on Saturday’s election, Adedamola called for a peaceful poll, urging political leaders, candidates and supporters to reject violence, intimidation and hate speech. “Osun State is bigger than any individual. Osun State is bigger than any political party. And Osun State is certainly bigger than any election. We must allow the people to exercise their democratic rights freely and peacefully,” he said Adedamola urged PDP members and structures across Osun to work towards the re-emergence of Governor Adeleke while conducting themselves lawfully and responsibly. items.title: After death of 3 Pakistani sailors, FO says Islamabad will implement maritime coalition 'in full earnest'
items.description: The Foreign Office (FO) said on Wednesday that Pakistan would implement the multinational maritime defence coalition “in full earnest”, after the deaths of three Pakistani sailors in strikes by Houthi rebels on a Saudi cargo ship on Tuesday. Last month, Saudi Arabia unveiled plans for a defence coalition to protect shipping and energy supply routes in the Red Sea region. The coalition was supported by 14 countries including Pakistan, Turkiye and Egypt in a joint statement. Answering questions at a weekly press briefing, FO spokesperson Tahir Andrabi said that Pakistan was a signatory of the recent joint statement supporting a multinational maritime defence coalition, led by Saudi Arabia, to protect shipping and energy supply routes. “Pakistan is a signatory to this maritime coalition communique and we will implement it with full earnest,” Andrabi said, adding that the country was engaged with the Saudi authorities in this regard. Andrabi further said that on the directions of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Pakistan was ascertaining the details of the agreement. In his opening statement, the FO also said that Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s visit to Iran was aimed at discussing bilateral relations, security-related matters and regional developments, particularly peace and stability in the region. He said Naqvi — who arrived in Tehran on Tuesday — was holding meetings with senior Iranian officials. He added that the visit provides the two countries the opportunity to discuss “bilateral relations, security-related matters, and regional development, with a particular focus on efforts to promote peace, stability, and constructive engagement amongst the parties in the region and regional developments”. Naqvi was received in Tehran by his Iranian counterpart, Eskandar Momeni, and later held talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Iranian media reported. A diplomatic source had told Dawn from Tehran that the principal objective of Naqvi’s visit was to follow up on the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding and Pakistan’s mediation bet­­w­een Iran and the US. Speaking further on Pakistan’s mediation efforts between the US and Iran, Andrabi reiterated that Pakistan remained engaged alongside “brotherly states” in “sincere efforts” to work towards a resolution to the crisis. “Pakistan is making all-out efforts to bring the two parties to the negotiating table and the Islamabad MoU and pave the way for peace and stability in the region,” he said. He also warned that Pakistan would continue to “offset spoilers using direct and indirect channels” and ensure the continuation of constructive dialogue to resolve outstanding issues. During the Q&A session, responding to a question regarding the status of the Islamabad MoU, the spokesperson said, “Whenever the rationality for dialogue will overcome the logic of escalation, the template for peace is provided in the Islamabad MoU and Pakistan-Qatar joint statement.” The current deadline for the 60-day period for US-Iran negotiations under the Islamabad MoU is Aug 17. Andrabi, however, noted that this deadline “can always be extended” if there is the intention to hold dialogue. “Even then, five days still remain, so we are not closing the chapter,” he added. “But we hope that even if the deadline is not implemented, the extension will take place eventually and the parties will revert to dialogue.” Asked about the basis for Pakistan’s continued optimism amid the US-Iran conflict, the spokesperson said, “As a mediator and facilitator of talks, we remain optimistic that a solution is in sight.” He pointed out that during the conflict, the countries had cycled through periods of heightened escalation followed by relative calm and eventual dialogue. He termed this “the natural progression of any armed conflict of international significance”. “We are not discouraged by escalations, as much as we do not get overly optimistic when there is a period of calm,” he said, while highlighting Pakistan’s sustained engagement with the parties to resolve the conflict. The country would continue its engagement with optimism “that ought to be there in any credible facilitator and mediator”, he added. Makkah pact reflects ‘resolve for sharing burden of regional peace’ The FO spokesperson also spoke of the defence pact signed last week between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, which he said was “highlight of the week”. The joint defence agreement, signed in Makkah on Friday, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them. He said the agreement reflected the three nations’ “commitment to further strengthen their collective security, promoting peace security and promoting peace security and stability in the region and beyond”. He said the agreement reflected the “long-standing brotherly relations” among the three countries and “displays our resolve for sharing the burden of regional peace and security”. “The agreement is purely defensive in nature and allows unified efforts to confront threats and security challenges to the member states,” Andrabi added, recalling Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar’s statement congratulating the nation on the agreement on August 10, wherein he held the agreement was defensive in nature and not against any country. Responding to a question, he noted that while the agreement was open to other countries, he was not “particularly aware” of which specific countries may join it in the future. He also said that he was not aware of any consultations with the US and China regarding the agreement, calling this “a matter of diplomatic exchange”, but noted that channels of communication with both countries remained open. FO rejects Indian MEA’s ‘baseless’ remarks on AJK When asked about the Indian Ministry of External Affairs’ recent remarks regarding alleged human rights abuses in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), the FO spokesperson rejected the “baseless” statement. The region has been gripped by unrest since early June as elections are also being held. “India’s professed concerns for human rights in AJK are disingenuous given its own well-documented record for repression in Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir, including excessive use of force, arbitrary detention, suppression of political freedom and sweeping powers under the draconian laws enacted there.” He added that India’s “politicisation” of developments in AJK was “misleading and cannot divert attention from the stark realities in Indian illegally occupied Kashmir”. “Pakistan remains fully committed to the protection of fundamental rights and the democratic freedom of AJK,” he said. He added that rather than making such statements over AJK, India would be “well advised to honour commitments made by its founding fathers and uphold the right of the people of Indian illegally occupied Jammu and Kashmir to freely determine their future through a United Nations plebiscite in accordance with relevant UN Security Council resolutions”.

items.title: Republic Bank JoyNews Habitat Fair: Lands Commission urges prospective homeowners to be careful of fraudsters
items.description: The Lands Commission is urging prospective homeowners to conduct thorough due diligence before purchasing land, warning that failure to verify ownership and register acquired property could expose buyers to fraud, double sales and costly litigation. The Commission, which is participating in the JoyNews Habitat Fair, says prospective homeowners must verify land ownership, conduct searches and ensure their transactions are properly registered before committing their hard-earned money. Acting Deputy Executive Secretary in charge of Operations at the Lands Commission, Surv. Raphael Hokey, says buyers must not treat land acquisition as an ordinary purchase because of the long-term financial implications involved. “The key thing to do is to make sure you carry out due diligence. And that involves visiting the land, asking for the site plan, contacting the Lands Commission, conducting a search, and doing other necessary things like asking around.” Mr Hokey says the risks are particularly significant given the nature of land ownership in Ghana, where a large proportion of land is held under customary ownership. “Ghana is an environment where about 80% of the land are customary lands. And so, family lands, stools, skin lands, individual lands, a mix of all that. If you are purchasing land and you don’t conduct the necessary search, you need to be sure you are dealing with the right person.” He says searches at the Lands Commission could take as little as a day in some cases, although more complex transactions may take longer. Mr Hokey is also warning buyers against sellers who refuse to provide site plans before payment, describing the practice as a major red flag. “Depending on the type of land, it can be as simple as a day’s information. And sometimes, if there are a lot of complexities around it, it may take a little while like a week or a month. Anybody who is the bonafide owner and is selling land will be comfortable and free to give you a site plan for you to go and conduct a search. Any time somebody is giving out land or selling land and he is unwilling to give you the site plan to go and do the necessary diligence, it means that there is a problem,” he mentioned. He further cautioned prospective homeowners against rushing into construction on land before completing the necessary legal and regulatory processes. According to him, acquiring land does not automatically give a buyer the right to begin construction, as the appropriate permits must first be secured. “Even if you have title, you will need to process your permit before you carry out construction. It is wrong to just get onto the land and start building because you will be breaching the laws of the assembly.” Mr Hokey is also urging landowners to register their properties after acquisition, saying registration provides an important record of ownership and can help protect buyers from subsequent claims. He says failure to register could leave buyers facing lengthy legal battles if the same property is subsequently sold to another person. “Your best assurance is to make sure that when you acquire land and you are given an indenture, you run to the Lands Commission to come and carry out the registration. If you do the registration, it is there, and it will serve as notice to the whole world,”he added. The Lands Commission’s participation in the JoyNews Habitat Fair, alongside financial institutions, developers and other industry players, is expected to provide prospective homeowners with information on land acquisition, property registration, financing and other critical steps towards secure home ownership.

items.title: OM : Nayef Aguerd passe sa visite médicale à la Real Sociedad
items.description: Nayef Aguerd se rapproche encore un peu plus de la sortie à l’Olympique de Marseille. Selon les informations de Foot Mercato, le défenseur marocain passe ce mercredi sa visite médicale à la Real Sociedad, où il devrait s’engager dans le cadre d’un prêt avec option d’achat. Le départ de Nayef Aguerd de l’Olympique de Marseille se précise. Alors que le club phocéen poursuit son opération dégraissage durant ce mercato estival, le défenseur central marocain est désormais tout proche de retrouver la Real Sociedad. Selon les informations de Foot Mercato, Nayef Aguerd passe sa visite médicale ce mercredi au sein du club espagnol. Une étape déterminante avant la finalisation de son arrivée, alors qu’un accord de principe a déjà été trouvé entre l’OM et la formation basque. Marseille et la Real Sociedad se sont entendus sur les bases d’un prêt avec option d’achat. Il ne reste donc plus que quelques détails à régler avant de voir le transfert devenir officiel. Le défenseur marocain connaît particulièrement bien la Real Sociedad. Il avait déjà porté les couleurs du club lors de la saison 2024-2025, avant de rejoindre Marseille. Son retour à Saint-Sébastien pourrait ainsi lui permettre de retrouver un environnement qu’il connaît et dans lequel il avait laissé une bonne impression. Arrivé à l’Olympique de Marseille avec l’ambition de renforcer la défense phocéenne, Aguerd s’apprête donc déjà à tourner la page marseillaise. items.title: Saisine rejetée par la CC : Les avocats pointent un « grave dysfonctionnement » parlementaire
items.description: La décision de la Cour constitutionnelle de déclarer son impossibilité de statuer, en l’état, sur la saisine relative à la conformité à la Constitution de la loi n° 66.23 portant organisation de la profession d’avocat continue de susciter des réactions. L’Association des barreaux du Maroc estime que cette situation engage directement la responsabilité de la présidence de la Chambre des représentants, considérant que l’irrégularité relevée ne saurait être assimilée à une simple erreur de procédure. Dans sa décision, la Cour constitutionnelle a constaté son impossibilité de se prononcer sur la saisine et a ordonné la notification de celle-ci au Chef du gouvernement, au président de la Chambre des représentants ainsi qu’au président de la Chambre des conseillers, avant sa publication au Bulletin officiel. La juridiction fonde sa position sur l’absence, dans la lettre de saisine transmise par le président de la Chambre des représentants, du texte de loi tel qu’adopté par la Chambre des conseillers lors de sa deuxième lecture du 7 juillet 2026. Pour Maitre Houcine Ziani, président de l’Association des barreaux du Maroc, cette affaire ne remet nullement en cause la Cour constitutionnelle. « La position de l’Association à l’égard de la Cour constitutionnelle est claire, et consiste en un respect total de cette institution ainsi que de ses jugements et décisions », a-t-il déclaré à Hespress au lendemain de la publication de la décision. Selon lui, la question soulevée concerne avant tout le processus ayant conduit à la saisine. « Le problème ne concerne pas la Cour constitutionnelle, qui assume sa mission de contrôle de conformité des textes à la Constitution de 2011, mais le cheminement de la saisine qui lui a été adressée et le degré de respect, par l’institution législative, des règles constitutionnelles et légales encadrant cette procédure », a-t-il expliqué. Le responsable s’interroge ainsi sur les circonstances ayant conduit à la transmission d’un dossier incomplet à la juridiction constitutionnelle. « Comment l’institution législative, représentée par le Parlement et la présidence de la Chambre des représentants, peut-elle saisir la Cour constitutionnelle afin qu’elle examine la conformité d’une loi à la Constitution alors que l’acte de saisine n’était pas accompagné du texte tel qu’adopté par la seconde Chambre lors de sa deuxième lecture ? », questionne-t-il. Une obligation constitutionnelle, selon l’Association Pour l’Association des barreaux, la responsabilité de l’institution législative ne se limite pas à prendre acte des décisions de la justice constitutionnelle. Elle englobe également le respect scrupuleux des procédures qui conditionnent l’exercice de ses prérogatives. « L’institution législative est tenue d’achever le processus législatif conformément à la Constitution et à la loi organique relative à la Cour constitutionnelle », souligne Maitre Ziani, estimant que « la résolution de cette situation ne se limite pas au respect des décisions rendues par la justice constitutionnelle ; elle commence avant tout par le respect des règles qui régissent l’exercice de ses compétences et des procédures encadrant la saisine » . Dans cette perspective, le président de l’Association considère que la correction de cette irrégularité « n’est plus un choix politique ni une simple formalité administrative », mais « une obligation constitutionnelle et institutionnelle qui s’impose au Parlement dans ses deux Chambres ». À ses yeux, les conclusions de la Cour soulèvent des interrogations de fond. « Ce à quoi est parvenue la Cour constitutionnelle, au regard de la nature du dysfonctionnement ayant empêché l’examen de la saisine, soulève de sérieuses questions qui ne peuvent être ignorées ou réduites à une simple omission procédurale », affirme-t-il. Maitre Ziani insiste sur le caractère particulièrement sensible de la procédure en cause. « Il s’agit d’une procédure constitutionnelle rigoureuse qui suppose, de la part de l’institution législative et des responsables chargés de sa gestion, une parfaite maîtrise de ses dispositions, de ses règles et des conséquences liées à leur non-respect », déclare-t-il. Tout en précisant que l’Association ne souhaite pas anticiper les développements à venir, il estime que « la Chambre des représentants a commis une faute grave dans le processus de saisine » et que « la nature de ce manquement ne permet pas de le considérer comme un simple incident procédural ». Des explications réclamées à la présidence de la Chambre Le président de l’Association juge nécessaire de déterminer précisément les circonstances ayant conduit à cette situation et les responsabilités institutionnelles qui en découlent. « Cette situation impose de faire toute la lumière sur ce qui s’est produit et de déterminer les responsabilités institutionnelles qui en résultent », soutient-il, ajoutant que « l’intégrité de la procédure constitutionnelle ne peut être laissée à l’appréciation des acteurs ni faire l’objet d’une application sélective ». Selon lui, les règles encadrant la saisine de la Cour constitutionnelle ne peuvent être considérées comme de simples dispositions facultatives. « Elles ne sauraient devenir des prescriptions dont il serait possible de s’affranchir ou de ne pas respecter les exigences », insiste-t-il. Le responsable relie également l’importance de cette affaire à la nature du texte concerné. La loi en question encadre une profession directement liée aux droits de la défense et aux garanties du procès équitable. Pour cette raison, « le respect des règles constitutionnelles et procédurales encadrant l’adoption du texte et sa transmission à la Cour ne souffre aucune approximation ». Dans ce contexte, Maitre Ziani estime que « la responsabilité institutionnelle impose aujourd’hui au président de la Chambre des représentants d’apporter des explications à l’opinion publique sur ce qui s’est réellement passé, d’identifier l’origine du dysfonctionnement et d’en préciser les circonstances ». Il considère par ailleurs que la réponse à apporter ne peut se limiter à constater l’irrégularité. « Il ne s’agit pas seulement d’enregistrer l’existence d’un dysfonctionnement, mais également de prendre l’initiative de le corriger, de l’expliquer et de procéder à une nouvelle saisine conforme aux exigences constitutionnelles et légales », affirme-t-il. Une responsabilité partagée avec le gouvernement L’Association des barreaux indique suivre de près l’évolution du dossier et précise que son bureau adoptera « les positions appropriées à la lumière des développements à venir ». Pour Maitre Ziani, l’incident est d’autant plus préoccupant qu’il concerne une institution investie du pouvoir législatif. « Une institution constitutionnelle chargée d’élaborer les lois du pays et des citoyens ne devrait pas commettre un tel manquement », déclare-t-il, rappelant au passage que « des doutes quant à la constitutionnalité de cette loi subsistent ». Il insiste également sur le fait que la Cour constitutionnelle ne s’est pas prononcée sur le fond du texte. « La justice constitutionnelle ne s’est pas prononcée sur la conformité ou l’inconstitutionnalité de la loi ; elle s’est trouvée dans l’impossibilité de l’examiner en raison du vice procédural qui a affecté la saisine », précise-t-il. Enfin, le président de l’Association ne limite pas la responsabilité de la situation actuelle au seul Parlement. Selon lui, « la responsabilité est désormais partagée entre le Parlement et le gouvernement ». Il adresse à cet égard une critique à l’Exécutif, qu’il accuse d’avoir enfreint le principe de l’approche participative. Tout en affirmant que l’Association ne cherche ni à intervenir dans le processus législatif ni à orienter les institutions dans l’exercice de leurs compétences, Maitre Ziani considère que la saisine transmise à la Cour « constitue, au-delà d’une saisine blanche, une saisine entachée d’irrégularités procédurales ». Il conclut que « cette situation résulte d’un dysfonctionnement imputable à l’institution parlementaire, en particulier à sa première Chambre, qui était chargée de transmettre le texte ». The post Saisine rejetée par la CC : Les avocats pointent un « grave dysfonctionnement » parlementaire appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Osun election: INEC includes SDP on ballot, reprints result sheets
items.description: Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it has included the Social Democratic Party (SDP) in the ballot for Saturday’s governorship election. Mohammed Haruna, INEC National Commissioner, Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee, stated this in a statement issued on Wednesday in Abuja. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that SDP is fielding Dr Francis Ajala and Faseke Oladipo as its governorship and deputy governorship candidates in the election. Haruna also stated that the commission was already reprinting ballot papers and results sheets for the exercise. He said that the action was taken in compliance with the judgment of the Federal High Court, Abuja, delivered on July 22 in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/344/2026 between SDP and Ajala against INEC. Haruna noted the court had ordered the commission to forthwith recognise, accept, upload, process and publish the name and particulars of Ajala as the SDP candidate for the governorship election. “Consequently, the ballot papers for the election, scheduled to hold on Saturday, Aug. 15, are being reproduced to reflect this addition, bringing to 15 the total number of political parties contesting the election. “The result sheets for the election are also being reproduced alongside the ballot papers to reflect the inclusion of the SDP candidate,” he said. Haruna stated that the reproduced ballot papers would arrive in Osun on Aug. 13 and would, on the same day, be moved to the commission’s local government area offices across the state, in line with its standard distribution procedure ahead of the election. “INEC assures political parties, candidates and the general public of its commitment to conducting a free, fair, and credible election in Osun,’’ he said. The post Osun election: INEC includes SDP on ballot, reprints result sheets appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Eclipse: « Il ne faut jamais regarder directement le Soleil », alerte Maram Kaïré
items.description: À Dakar, l’Agence sénégalaise d’études spatiales (Aspa) prévoit, cette après-midi, une séance publique d’observation sur la Corniche Ouest, au niveau de la plateforme située en face de la Bibliothèque universitaire (Bu) de l’Université Cheikh Anta Diop de Dakar (Ucad). Le site a notamment été choisi pour son horizon ouest dégagé. « Nos équipes seront présentes avec des équipements adaptés pour permettre au public d’observer le phénomène en toute sécurité, mais aussi pour expliquer et répondre aux questions », annonce Maram Kaïré, directeur général de l’Agence sénégalaise d’études spatiales (Aspa). Une précaution s’impose toutefois : l’observation directe du soleil sans protection adaptée peut être dangereuse pour les yeux. « Il ne faut jamais regarder directement le soleil sans une protection spécialement conçue pour l’observation solaire », a-t-il conseillé. Toutefois, les lunettes de soleil ordinaires ne constituent pas une protection suffisante. B. G. DIOP

items.title: Legal vacation: Ayikoi Otoo says compelling lawyers to appear in court is unfair
items.description: Former Attorney General and former Ghana High Commissioner to the United Kingdom, Ayikoi Otoo, has criticised the decision to compel lawyers to appear in court during the legal vacation, describing the practice as unfair and something that should only happen in exceptional circumstances. According to Mr Otoo, while the High Court rules may give the Chief Justice the authority to issue directions concerning court sittings during the legal vacation, such powers should be exercised sparingly and with regard to established legal practice. Speaking on the Joy FM Super Morning Show on Wednesday, August 12, amid the controversy over the legal vacation, Mr Otoo said he was not aware of a practice where lawyers, particularly those involved in high-profile cases, were routinely directed to continue with hearings during the break. “I am not very conversant with that kind of practice, although in the High Court rules, you will find that the Chief Justice can give directions, including vacations. But I am not very, very conversant, to be very, very honest with you. I don’t remember these things happening,” he said. Mr Otoo, who was called to the Bar in 1981 and practised law for about 45 years, said the legal profession had traditionally recognised the vacation as a period when lawyers were entitled to take a break from court proceedings. He questioned why lawyers should be forced back into court simply because a particular case was considered important or there was pressure to conclude it quickly. “I agree with Atta Akyea. You can’t compel him. What you are doing is that you are compelling him to go to the court, to the extent that you are saying if he’s not there, his clients will be compelled to do cross-examination,” he said. “Are they lawyers? Why did they go for a lawyer? The people have gone to hire a lawyer, the lawyer is on legal vacation, and you are saying that if they don’t come, then the lawyers should be compelled to hear. We should stop what we are doing. I think it is simply not fair.” Mr Otoo said the legal vacation exists to give members of the legal profession an opportunity to rest, saying that the need to conclude individual cases should not automatically override that arrangement. “We are entitled to go and rest and come after the legal vacation. So why do you compel him to go to court? Because somebody is interested in concluding a particular case,” he said. “Why can’t we wait for two months for people to rest and come back to continue the hearing?” Mr Otoo said his own experience over more than four decades in the legal profession had not exposed him to a situation where Chief Justices routinely directed lawyers to appear during the legal vacation, particularly in high-profile cases. “I was called to the Bar in 1981. I practised law for about 45 years,” he said. “I said I don’t have this experience of Chief Justices directing people to hear cases during vacations, especially with such high-profile cases. What message are you sending out there?” This follows complaints from three law firms regarding notices directing their lawyers to appear before judges to continue hearing part-heard criminal cases during the current legal vacation. The Ghana Bar Association (GBA) appealed to Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie to ensure that judges uphold the established rules and traditions governing Ghana’s legal vacation, particularly in cases where lawyers have indicated that they are unavailable to appear in court. But the Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie rejected the position that lawyers can decline to proceed with cases simply because they have been scheduled during the legal vacation.

items.title: Trade unions must move beyond workers’ demands, embrace institutional partnerships for justice delivery – Labour Minister
items.description: The Minister of Labour, Employment and Jobs, Abdul-Rashid Pelpuo, has called on trade unions to move beyond their traditional focus on wages, allowances and conditions of service and embrace a more progressive approach that prioritises institutional development and quality service delivery. According to him, modern trade unionism must position workers’ organisations as responsible partners in improving productivity, among others. He made the call at the 2nd Quadrennial Delegates’ Congress of the Senior Staff Association of the Judicial Service of Ghana (SSAJUG) in Sunyani, on the theme, “Trade Unionism in the Service: Partnering Management for Quality Justice Administration.” Mr Pelpuo said the theme was particularly relevant to Ghana’s democracy, industrial relations and justice delivery. “The theme challenges us to move beyond our traditional understanding of trade unionism as being primarily about wages, allowances and conditions of service,” he said. He argued that unions should no longer be viewed primarily as defenders of workers against management, but as “a partner in institutional development, productivity, ethical conduct, innovation, accountability and quality service delivery.” The Minister, however, also urged management to change its perception of trade unions, stressing that workers’ organisations should not be regarded as obstacles to efficiency. “Progressive management must not regard the trade union as an obstacle to efficiency. Rather, it must view the trade union as an important institutional partner, source of knowledge, early warning mechanism and stakeholder in organisational transformation,” he said. He emphasised that the rights of workers must be exercised alongside responsibilities, particularly within the Judicial Service, whose work has direct implications for public confidence in justice. He cited concerns over delays and alleged unethical conduct within the justice system, where he recounted a case brought to his attention in which a litigant was reportedly informed that documents relating to his case had been misplaced. “The judicial service is not an ordinary public institution,” he said. “It is one of the pillars upon which our constitutional democracy rests.” He therefore challenged SSAJUG members to advocate not only for better working conditions but also for excellence, professionalism, and integrity. The Minister further urged unions to exercise restraint when negotiations over their demands do not yield immediate results, warning that industrial action could compound challenges facing institutions and the general economy of the country. He therefore called for greater collaboration between workers, management and government, insisting that quality justice administration depends heavily on the competence, conduct and commitment of the people who operate the justice system. “Justice is not just about the law; it is also about the process, and it is also about the person who delivers the process,” Mr Pelpuo said. Meanwhile, SSAJUG President, Maureen Suttah Marilyn, has stressed that “no workforce can deliver excellent results when it appears that there is a perpetual uncertainty about ever attaining decent working conditions.” She recounted a worrying trend in which a significant number of staff, including competent senior officers, had left the service over the past three years to seek greener pastures abroad. “My Lord, while we remain grateful, especially for the coming into force of CI 141 during your tenure of office, may I respectfully use this opportunity to humbly plead with you to ensure the implementation of the CI and the conclusion of salary negotiations for 2027 before you leave office,” she appealed. She said fulfilling the request would be something for which members of the service would remain eternally grateful to the Chief Justice. She also appealed for the refurbishment of courthouses to provide staff of the service with a more conducive working environment, adding that “some of the courts are in quite an unsatisfactory state.”

items.title: Éducation en Algérie : pourquoi soustraire le français quand on peut additionner l’anglais ?
items.description: CONTRIBUTION . Alors que le ministère de l'Éducation nationale accentue le remplacement du français par l'anglais dès le primaire, le débat sur la place des langues étrangères refait surface. Entre passions identitaires et réalités du terrain, l'Algérie a tout à gagner à privilégier l'addition des savoirs plutôt que la soustraction des compétences. Le ministère de l’Éducation nationale a pris une mesure d'envergure en retirant le français du programme de 3ᵉ année primaire au profit de l’anglais, qui devient ainsi l'unique langue étrangère enseignée à ce niveau. Cette décision importante a aussitôt ravivé le débat historique et idéologique sur la place de la langue française en Algérie. D'un côté, les partisans d'une arabisation renforcée y voient une étape logique et nécessaire, permettant à l’Algérie de s'affranchir définitivement de la langue de l'ancien colonisateur. Ils perçoivent dans l'omniprésence du français une forme de dépendance culturelle, voire l'ombre d'une ingérence étrangère. D'un autre côté, les franges les plus francophiles estiment que cette décision risque de freiner le développement du pays, allant parfois jusqu'à attribuer à la langue arabe l'origine des difficultés socio-éducatives de l'Algérie. La souveraineté face à l'épreuve du réel Pour ma part, je ne partage ni la posture des premiers, ni le radicalisme des seconds. Certes, l’Algérie est un État souverain, pleinement légitime à définir ses choix politiques et éducatifs sans rendre de comptes à des tiers. Néanmoins, il est permis de s’interroger sur l’opportunité d'une telle mesure pour l’avenir des générations futures. Lors d'une récente visite à l’hôpital de Kouba (Alger), j'ai pu constater que le personnel médical s’exprimait majoritairement en français, que les comptes rendus de soins et les ordonnances y étaient rédigés dans cette langue et que la signalétique y demeurait francophone. Ce constat du terrain soulève trois questions fondamentales : 1 – Sur l'identité et le statut : L’éviction progressive du français répond-elle véritablement à la sauvegarde de l’identité algérienne (islam, arabité, amazighité), ou revient-elle à se priver d'un « butin de guerre « , selon la célèbre formule de Kateb Yacine (« Le Polygone étoilé « , Éditions du Seuil, 1966) et d'un outil d'ouverture déjà ancré dans la société ? 2 – Sur le terrain et le pragmatisme : Peut-on décréter la fin d'une langue par voie administrative alors qu'elle demeure, comme à l'hôpital et à l’université, la langue de travail et de transmission dans des secteurs scientifiques et techniques vitaux ? 3 – Sur la transition et la souveraineté : Le système éducatif dispose-t-il des ressources pédagogiques nécessaires pour réussir le passage à l'anglais sans créer un vide linguistique ni fragiliser le niveau académique des élèves ? Additionner les savoirs plutôt que les soustraire En réalité , le véritable enjeu pour l’Algérie de demain ne réside pas dans le remplacement d’une langue par une autre, mais dans la capacité à former des générations véritablement multilingues. L'émancipation nationale et la souveraineté ne s'obtiennent pas en restreignant le champ des connaissances, mais en accumulant les savoirs. L'arabe et l'amazighité constituent le socle inaliénable de l’identité algérienne ; l'anglais est la clef incontournable des sciences et de la mondialisation ; et le français demeure un héritage historique et un outil de communication précieux. En dépassant les querelles idéologiques au profit d'un pragmatisme pédagogique, l'Algérie peut faire du pluralisme linguistique non pas une source de division, mais une force stratégique au service de son développement. *Azzédine Gaci est recteur de la mosquée de Villeurbanne Important : Les tribunes publiées sur TSA ont pour but de permettre aux lecteurs de participer au débat. Elles ne reflètent pas la position de la rédaction de notre média. L’article Éducation en Algérie : pourquoi soustraire le français quand on peut additionner l’anglais ? est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Última hora del eclipse solar de agosto en España, en directo | Cataluña avisa de un aumento de tráfico ante el eclipse y Castilla-La Mancha pide evitar desplazamientos con un Es-Alert
items.description: Cataluña ha detectado desde ayer martes un aumento de los desplazamientos hacia las Terres de l’Ebre, una de las zonas donde el eclipse solar se podrá observar en mejores condiciones. La consejera de Interior de la Generalitat, Núria Parlon, ha destacado esta mañana el incremento de los viajes también en transporte público. En Castilla-La Mancha, Protección Civil ha enviado un mensaje Es-Alert a los móviles pidiendo evitar desplazamientos innecesarios y no detenerse en los arcenes. La DGT estima que pueden producirse hasta 1,5 millones de desplazamientos adicionales para llegar a las zonas donde poder observar el eclipse solar que cruzará la Península y será total solo en una franja que la atraviesa de oeste a este, incluyendo varias capitales de provincia desde A Coruña hasta Palma. Comenzará a partir de las 19.30 y terminará poco antes de las 21.30. Las autoridades de Consumo de varias comunidades autónomas han ordenado la retirada del mercado de un nuevo modelo de gafas por riesgo de lesiones oculares, por lo que ya son siete los modelos retirados: Mó, Lionstar, ECP Eye Care Proffesional, Pelispan, Homanaje, Orro y Opticalia. Algunas comunidades han alertado del riesgo de incendios por las altas temperaturas y han pedido a quienes planeen acudir a zonas de campo y bosque máxima precaución. EL PAÍS ha recopilado casi 500 miradores oficiales donde poder observar esa noche durante el día, que durará menos de dos minutos. Una vez que se ponga el sol, podrá verse otro fenómeno, aunque este más habitual (se repite cada verano): la lluvia de estrellas de las Perseidas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Tone/éducation : Un projet lancé pour améliorer l’accès et le maintien des enfants à l’école
items.description: Dapaong, 12 août. (ATOP) – Le projet « Amélioration de l’accès et du maintien à l’école pour les enfants du Bénin et du Togo : toutes et tous à l’école » a été lancé au terme d’un atelier les 11 et 12 août à Dapaong. Ce projet est initié par l’ONG Action éducation, autrefois Aide et action, en collaboration avec le ministère de l’Education nationale et celui des Solidarités, du Genre, de la Famille et de la Protection de l’enfance. Il bénéficie du soutien de l’Agence française de développement (AFD). Le but est de contribuer à l’éducation pour tous, surtout dans les Savanes au Togo, où le taux d’enfants de 6 à 11 ans non scolarisés est de 34 %. On y dénombre aussi plus de 61.000 personnes déplacées qui créent une énorme pression sur les écoles locales. D’une durée de quatre ans, le projet sera mis en œuvre dans 250 écoles primaires des communes de Cinkassé 2, Kpendjal 2, Kpendjal ouest 1, Oti sud 1 et Tandjouaré 2. Il va garantir l’accès et le maintien de plus de 17.000 enfants à l’école. Plus précisément, 14.830 enfants hors écoles seront insérés ou réinsérés dans le système éducatif et 2.510 élèves à risque de décrochage seront maintenus sur les bancs. Une première phase de deux ans va permettre d’abord d’insérer 6.351 enfants et de maintenir 1.242 élèves. Il est prévu, en outre, des aménagements, des classes de rattrapage et des services adaptés aux enfants handicapés et à ceux déplacés. Le financement de ce projet pour le Togo s’élève à plus de 1.350.000.000 FCFA, dont 809 000 000 FCFA pour les deux premières années. L’atelier de lancement a été consacré à la planification opérationnelle du projet et à la définition des orientations stratégiques. Les participants ont analysé le mécanisme de suivi-évaluation, de redevabilité et de gestion de risques et mis en place une feuille de route consensuelle de démarrage opérationnel du projet d’ici la prochaine rentrée scolaire. Le gouverneur de la région des Savanes, Atcha-Dédji Affoh a exprimé sa gratitude à l’ONG Action éducation pour ce projet qui est en adéquation avec les priorités fondamentales de l’éducation au Togo. Pour lui, c’est un levier pour la promotion d’une véritable équité entre les filles et les garçons, la lutte contre les obstacles socioculturels et économiques qui freinent encore la scolarisation des enfants et l’insertion des enfants vivant avec un handicap. Le gouverneur a exhorté chaque acteur à s’impliquer dans la mise en œuvre de ce projet pour sa réussite. Le directeur pays Togo de l’ONG Action éducation, Narzoume Tchingue a indiqué que le projet ambitionne de garantir le droit à une éducation inclusive et de qualité dans les Savanes. « Ce n’est pas seulement un devoir social. C’est un impératif de résilience face aux crises sécuritaires et économiques que traverse la région. Le projet ne laisse personne de côté, ni les enfants des familles démunies, ni les enfants handicapés, ni les enfants déplacés », a-t-il déclaré. ATOP/TKA/JK/MD

items.title: Heads of Special Schools calls for incentives to recruit and retain specialised teachers in Ghana’s special schools
items.description: The Conference of Heads of Special Schools (COHESS) is calling on the government to introduce stronger incentives and support systems to attract, train and retain specialised teachers in special schools across the country. The organisation says about 70% of teachers currently working in special schools are regular teachers who require additional training to effectively respond to the unique educational needs of learners with disabilities. COHESS, which serves as a bridge between special schools and institutions including the Ghana Education Service (GES) and the Ministry of Education, says the shortage of specialised teachers remains one of the major challenges confronting education for persons with disabilities. While acknowledging government efforts to improve education for persons living with disabilities, including the introduction of free tertiary education for eligible students, the organisation says more needs to be done to address the critical human resource gap. Speaking to the media, National Chairperson of COHESS, Rosaline Fimpomaa Adjepong, said the situation was becoming increasingly difficult as experienced special educators leave the system. “The special educators that we have in our schools, most of them are now moving out. We have regular teachers who are not special educators in our schools, and in fact, it’s difficult because before they are even able to learn to sign or learn Braille or learn to communicate with children with intellectual and developmental disabilities, it takes time,” she said. She appealed to the government to introduce specific measures to motivate teachers working in special schools. “I’m pleading that teacher motivation is put in place,” she added. According to COHESS, specialised educators require skills such as sign language, Braille and other specialised communication techniques to effectively teach learners with different disabilities. The organisation says the time required to train regular teachers in these skills can affect the delivery of education, particularly where schools are already understaffed. Ms Adjepong also raised concerns about the limited availability of allied health professionals who support learners with intellectual and developmental disabilities. “When you come to schools for the IDD, we need speech therapists, we need occupational therapists, we need physiotherapists, and we don’t have these in our schools,” she said. She said the absence of such professionals further limits the ability of special schools to provide comprehensive support for learners. The concerns were raised at the 43rd Annual Conference of the Conference of Heads of Special Schools in Ghana, where COHESS presented key challenges facing special schools and called for urgent government intervention. Responding to the concerns, Deputy Director-General of the Ghana Education Service, Professor Smile Gavua, assured COHESS that steps would be taken to address staffing challenges in special schools. She said the GES was committed to providing the resources required by special schools and improving the recruitment of persons with disabilities into the education system. “We are not joking with whatever resources that they need. Recently, we have met with the association of persons with disabilities. The concerns that they have with their recruitment, we are addressing it,” she said. Professor Gavua said the GES also wanted to make the education system more inclusive by employing more persons with disabilities. She explained that their presence in schools could provide children with disabilities with role models and mentors who understand their experiences. “We want to make them very comfortable. We want to absorb them into the system so they’ll be good role models, good mentors for other children with a disability as well,” she said. COHESS is now hoping that the GES assurance will translate into concrete measures to close the staffing gap, strengthen specialised teaching and ultimately improve learning outcomes for students with special educational needs.

items.title: Tchad : interdiction de la commercialisation et la consommation du produit « Coloss »
items.description: © (DR) Le ministère du Commerce a produit un communiqué ce 12 août pour interdire la consommation du produit en sachet "Collorado" plus connu sous l'appellation "Coloss" D'après le département, ce produit vendu en sachet sous la dénomination « COLORADO », communément appelé « COLOSS », est identifié comme un stupéfiant à effets psychotropes, dont la consommation est susceptible de porter atteinte à la santé et la sécurité de la population. En conséquence, l'importation, la distribution, la détention, la vente et la consommation de ce produit sous quelque forme que ce soit, sont formellement interdites sur l'ensemble du territoire national. "Tout contrevenant s'expose aux sanctions prévues par les textes en vigueur, prévient le ministre du commerce. Il exhorte la population à ne pas acheter, détenir ni consommer ce produit, à faire preuve de vigilance et à signaler aux services compétents tout point de vente, lieu de stockage ou toute personne impliquée dans l'importation, la distribution, la détention, la commercialisation ou la consommation dudit produit. Le ministère dit réaffirmer son engagement à protéger la santé et la sécurité des populations et à prendre toutes les mesures nécessaires pour garantir la sécurité et la conformité des produits mis sur le marché national. items.title: Norwegian FM to visit Pakistan on Aug 13-14, first such visit in a decade
items.description: Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide will undertake an official visit to Pakistan on August 13-14 to discuss avenues for expanding bilateral cooperation, trade and investment. In a statement, the Foreign Office (FO) said, “At the invitation of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Norwegian FM Eide will undertake an official visit to Pakistan on 13-14 August 2026.” According to the FO, the visit to Pakistan will be the first by a Norwegian foreign minister in a decade. During the visit, the FO said that Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and his Norwegian counterpart would hold delegation-level talks covering the full spectrum of Pakistan-Norway relations. “The two sides will discuss avenues for further expanding bilateral cooperation, particularly in trade and investment, climate change, renewable energy, education and people-to-people contacts. “They will also exchange views on important regional and international developments,” it added. FM Eide has appreciated and acknowledged Pakistan’s efforts to de-escalate tensions in the region through mediation during the US-Israeli war on Iran. The FO stated that the visit would provide an opportunity to “further strengthen the longstanding and cordial relations between Pakistan and Norway and to explore new areas of mutually beneficial cooperation”. During his visit to Norway in May, FM Dar also had a meeting with Norwegian deputy foreign minister and discussed the regional situation with him.

items.title: Groups reject Foreign Aid Bill, urge Senate to withdraw it
items.description: ABUJA — Five human rights organisations have called on the National Assembly and the Federal Government to withdraw the Foreign Aids (Regulation, Transparency and Disclosure) Bill, 2026 (SB. 1034), warning that its provisions could restrict civic space and undermine the work of human rights defenders and civil society organisations. The organisations are the Nigerian Human Rights Defenders Network (NHRDN), Partnership for Justice, Front Line Defenders (FLD), West African Human Rights Defenders Network (WAHRDN) and Protection International (PI). In a joint statement issued on Wednesday, the groups said the bill, sponsored by Senator Ibrahim Hassan Dankwambo (PDP, Gombe North), had passed second reading in the Senate in July. They said the proposed legislation seeks to establish a Foreign Aid Regulatory Commission (FARC) with powers to register, inspect, audit, sanction and suspend or shut down organisations receiving foreign grants, donations or technical assistance. According to the organisations, the proposed regulatory framework could affect independent civic groups, human rights defenders, legal aid providers and humanitarian organisations operating in Nigeria. They argued that the bill was inconsistent with Nigeria’s commitments under the fourth cycle of the Universal Periodic Review (UPR), particularly recommendations relating to creating a safe and enabling environment for human rights defenders and civil society organisations. The groups also noted that Nigeria is a candidate for election to the United Nations Human Rights Council for the 2027-2029 term, saying the country’s candidacy should be accompanied by stronger domestic protection of human rights defenders. The organisations raised concerns over several provisions of the proposed legislation. They said Section 6(1), which requires foreign aid to be registered within 30 days of receipt, could create difficulties for emergency funding, including legal defence, relocation assistance and support for survivors of rights violations. The groups also criticised Sections 7 and 8, which provide for public disclosure of implementing partners and funded activities through a national register. They argued that public disclosure of information involving human rights defenders, survivors, witnesses and individuals involved in sensitive documentation could expose them to security risks. The organisations further raised concerns over Section 11, which requires foreign-funded activities to align with Nigeria’s national development plans and priorities. They described the provision as broad and potentially capable of affecting organisations working on human rights, land and environmental rights, and support for vulnerable communities. The groups also questioned the need for the proposed FARC, arguing that some of its functions could overlap with existing institutions, including the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC), Special Control Unit Against Money Laundering (SCUML), Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS) and Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU). The organisations called on the Senate, its leadership and the Federal Government to immediately withdraw the bill. They also urged the authorities to ensure that any future legislation regulating civic space and foreign funding complies with the Constitution, the UN Declaration on Human Rights Defenders and Nigeria’s international human rights obligations. The groups called for meaningful consultation with civil society organisations and human rights defenders in developing any future regulatory framework. They also demanded explicit legal protection for confidential information concerning human rights defenders, survivors, witnesses and other at-risk individuals receiving support through foreign funding. The organisations further called for an expedited framework for emergency and protection-related funding, including legal, medical, psychosocial and relocation support for defenders at risk. They urged the government to reaffirm constitutional guarantees on freedom of association, expression and assembly. While acknowledging the importance of transparency in the use of foreign funding, the organisations said regulatory mechanisms should not be used to restrict legitimate human rights activities. They urged the National Assembly to withdraw SB. 1034 and ensure that any future regulatory framework protects the civic space and those working to defend human rights in Nigeria. The post Groups reject Foreign Aid Bill, urge Senate to withdraw it appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Guan Congress 2026 to showcase tourism and investment opportunities in Anum
items.description: Media and Publicity Chair of the Local Organising Committee, Seth Adu Mensah, has said the Guan Congress Anum 2026 is expected to highlight tourism and investment opportunities in Anum as organisers seek to attract investors and visitors to the area. The congress, scheduled for Friday, August 14 to Sunday, August 16, will bring together Guan communities, traditional leaders, young people, investors and other stakeholders for a weekend of cultural, business and development activities. Speaking on the Joy Super Morning Show on Wednesday, August 12, Seth Adu Mensah, Media and Publicity Chair of the Local Organising Committee, said the event would provide an opportunity to showcase the economic potential of the area. “We want, after the Congress, to expose these potential investment opportunities to people so that people can get jobs, people can get employment, and people can develop themselves,” he said. Mr Mensah said Anum and surrounding communities have several tourism attractions that could be developed to support the local economy. He noted that the area has more than 20 tourist sites, some of which remain largely untapped. “We have a lot of tourist attractions within Anum. In fact, we have more than 22 tourist sites in there, which we cannot mention all of them here,” he said. As part of the congress event, participants will embark on a hiking expedition and other excursions to experience some of the area’s natural attractions. Mr Mensah said the activities were deliberately included to expose participants to the tourism potential of the area and encourage investment. He said the area’s location also presents opportunities for property development and other businesses, particularly with the construction of an inland port. “From property development, people can actually look at the investment opportunities within Anum. The inland port is now being constructed at this point, so there is a lot that can take this route,” he said. According to the organisers, greater investment in tourism, property development and related sectors could create employment opportunities for residents and contribute to the long-term development of the community. The congress is therefore expected to go beyond cultural celebrations by creating a platform for business networking, tourism promotion and investment. Organisers have invited investors interested in tourism and other sectors to participate in the congress and explore opportunities available in Anum. They also encouraged members of the public and people interested in experiencing Guan culture to attend the event. The organisers expressed the hope that the exposure generated by the congress would translate into concrete investments and development projects that would continue to benefit the community after the event.

items.title: Serial UK sex attacker jailed for life for double murder, rape after police failings
items.description: A British serial sex attacker was sentenced to spend the rest of his life in jail ​on Wednesday, after he was convicted of two murders and rape ‌following an escalating spree of sexual offences which police and prosecutors failed to stop. Simon Levy, 40, was found guilty last week of the murder of Carmenza Valencia-Trujillo in March 2025 ​and of Sheryl Wilkins in August 2025, as well as the rape ​and serious assault of a third woman in January that ⁠year. Police had arrested Levy several times for sexual assaults against women on ​rush-hours trains before he was again arrested on suspicion of murdering Valencia-Trujillo, 53, ​in April 2025. But Levy was released and sexually assaulted five women before he killed Wilkins, 39, in a brutal attack. Judge Mark Lucraft said Levy was “clearly someone who ruthlessly exploits others ​for your own personal, sexual satisfaction” as he sentenced him to a ​whole-life order without the possibility of parole for the murder of Valencia-Trujillo and Wilkins. He was also sentenced ‌for ⁠two counts of rape, causing grievous bodily harm with intent and intentional strangulation in relation to a third woman. Levy was separately convicted in February of sexually assaulting 10 women on London trains between October 2023 and May 2025, with ​six of the ​attacks in early ⁠2025, and an 11th charge of sexually assaulting a prison officer in April 2022. His crimes and the failures by ​police and prosecutors which allowed him to continue offending has ​prompted questions, ⁠while London’s Metropolitan Police has referred itself to the police watchdog for downgrading him to a medium-risk offender. “Time and time again, opportunities to stop him were ⁠missed,” London ​Mayor Sadiq Khan said in a statement. “I am ​appalled by his crimes and the failures across multiple agencies that could have prevented him from ​harming, and ultimately killing, more women.”

items.title: One dead, 172 rescued after Indonesian ferry from Bali catches fire
items.description: Indonesian authorities rescued 172 people on Wednesday after a ferry travelling from the ​tourist island of Bali caught fire in waters off ‌Lombok, officials said, as the search continued for any other missing passengers. The KM Putri Yasmin ferry left Padangbai port in Bali for Lembar port in Lombok in ​the province of West Nusa Tenggara, said Muhammad Hariyadi, the ​head of the local rescue agency. The incident took place in the Lombok ⁠Strait at 4:39 a.m. on Wednesday (2039 GMT Tuesday), Hariyadi told Reuters. By ​Wednesday afternoon, one Indonesian had been confirmed dead and 172 people had been evacuated ​to ports in Bali and Lombok, Hariyadi said. Of the survivors, one was Australian and the rest were Indonesian. “We have deployed some boats to carry out the evacuation and coordinate with other ​boats surrounding the location of the incident,” Hariyadi said, adding that more ​than 200 personnel had been deployed to handle the operation. It was unclear how the ‌ferry ⁠caught fire, or whether overcrowding was a factor. Earlier in the day, an official at Padangbai port in Bali, Heri Wiyanto, told local broadcaster Kompas TV that only 114 passengers and 17 crew were registered in the ferry’s ​manifest. The incident took ​place less ⁠than a month after another ferry, KM Mutiara Sentosa 2, caught fire off Madura island, killing five ​people. The vessel was also carrying more people than ​its ⁠manifest showed. Indonesia, an archipelago of 17,000 islands, relies heavily on ferries as a key mode of transportation, with sea routes more ⁠affordable and ​readily available than air travel. However, safety ​standards are not always rigorously enforced, resulting in a relatively high rate of ​accidents.

items.title: Forensic report on National Cathedral is ready, undergoing review – Kwakye Ofosu
items.description: Minister of State for Government Communications Felix Kwakye Ofosu has disclosed that the long-awaited forensic audit report into the National Cathedral is ready and has been submitted to the Attorney General for review. According to him, the Attorney General received the report last Friday and is currently studying its findings to determine the appropriate next steps. Speaking on Adom TV’s Badwam , Mr Kwakye Ofosu said the forensic audit became necessary after an earlier audit by Deloitte and Touche uncovered financial irregularities but did not establish the full extent of the issues or identify those responsible. “Deloitte and Touche audited the financial reports of the National Cathedral, which revealed financial irregularities, but it didn’t tell all the issues,” he said. He explained that authorities subsequently decided to conduct a forensic examination to establish who was responsible for the irregularities and determine whether the transactions were lawful. “So we had to go further and do the forensic audit to know the people who were responsible for those irregularities and whether it was lawful or not,” he said. Mr Kwakye Ofosu said the Attorney General authorised the Auditor-General to undertake the forensic audit, which has now been completed. “The Attorney General received the forensic audit report last Friday and is going through it to determine the next line of action,” he stated. He stressed that he had not personally seen the report and would not comment on its specific findings, as the appropriate time for such disclosures had not arrived. “I haven’t seen the report myself, and even if I have, I won’t speak to the issues because it is not time,” he said. According to him, the findings of the initial audit established that there were issues requiring further investigation, with the forensic audit expected to provide clarity on those responsible. “But the initial report revealed that something went wrong, so the forensic will prove those responsible,” he said. Mr Kwakye Ofosu maintained that no individual would be shielded if the forensic audit establishes wrongdoing. He added that the Attorney General would determine the appropriate legal action based on the findings of the report. “So if anyone is indicted, I won’t be the one to say who should face the law or not. Based on the report, the Attorney General will take the necessary steps,” he stated. He emphasised that the forensic audit will ultimately provide clarity on expenditures and ensure accountability for taxpayer funds spent on the project.

items.title: North Korea fires missile ahead of major US-South Korea drills
items.description: North Korea fired a ​ballistic missile on Wednesday toward the sea off the Korean Peninsula’s east coast, South Korean and Japanese authorities said, days ahead of major ‌joint military exercises by Seoul and Washington long denounced by Pyongyang. The missile was launched from the North’s Wonsan area at about 6 a.m. (2100 GMT Tuesday), South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) said, six days after North Korea fired another ballistic missile from the same area. The launch came ahead of South Korean and U.S. military drills, dubbed Ulchi Freedom Shield, set to run from August 17 to ​August 27, aimed at countering Pyongyang’s evolving nuclear and weapons capabilities. Hong Min, a senior researcher at the Korea Institute for National Unification in Seoul, ​said the launch was likely part of North Korea’s existing weapons development schedule, but the timing could also have been selected ⁠to send a message ahead of the exercises. “Even if it was a test of a weapon under development, choosing when to conduct it requires a political decision,” ​Hong said. There was no immediate statement from North Korea on the Wonsan launch, but Pyongyang on Wednesday afternoon criticised the nuclear ambitions of South Korea and Japan. South Korea ​said North Korea also fired a ballistic missile from Wonsan on August 6, but Pyongyang did not report that launch in state media. Hong said that test may have failed to achieve its intended objective. North Korea’s series of tests this year has featured short-range ballistic missiles, artillery rockets and other tactical weapons. Wednesday’s launch was its 11th suspected ballistic missile test in 2026, according to ​South Korean assessments. South Korean and Japanese defence authorities said the missile flew about 700 km (435 miles). Seoul’s Joint Chiefs of Staff did not identify it as a short-range ​ballistic missile, saying authorities would conduct a detailed analysis. The omission leaves open the question of what type of missile it was, analysts said. Ballistic missiles with ranges of 300 km to ‌1,000 km (186 ⁠miles to 620 miles) are generally classified as short-range. Hong said the range, trajectory and launch site suggested it may have been a type of hypersonic missile, though a submarine-launched missile was also possible. CONDEMNATION AND HEIGHTENED TENSIONS South Korea and Japan both condemned the launch. “Japan lodged a strong protest with North Korea through diplomatic channels at the Japanese Embassy in Beijing and strongly condemned the action,” Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi told reporters. South Korea’s Office of National Security convened an emergency meeting and expressed concern over ​North Korea’s continued ballistic-missile launches following the ​August 6 firing. It urged Pyongyang ⁠to halt provocations that violate U.N. Security Council resolutions. South Korea’s military said it was maintaining readiness to respond “overwhelmingly” to any provocation under its combined defence posture with the United States. The U.S. Indo-Pacific Command said it was consulting closely with allies and ​partners, adding that its initial assessment was that the launch posed no immediate threat to U.S. personnel or territory, or ​to its allies. On Tuesday, ⁠Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Moscow used North Korean ballistic missiles during a Russian attack that killed seven workers at a steel plant in the southeastern city of Zaporizhzhia. In a statement, a North Korean Foreign Ministry official responsible for South Korean affairs said Seoul’s plans to develop nuclear-powered submarines would heighten instability in the region, for a “serious challenge” to the ⁠North’s security. Pyongyang ​needed the capability to counter its adversaries’ military moves with retaliatory strikes that would make their “survival and ​recovery impossible”, the statement added. In a separate commentary state news agency KCNA accused Japan of seeking nuclear weapons under the guise of peaceful use of atomic energy, citing its nuclear power programme and debate ​among Japanese politicians over nuclear armament.

items.title: PM takes notice of future after ordering it cancelled
items.description: I have spent the better part of two decades trying to persuade Pakistan’s institutions to think in decades rather than in news cycles. I built the Pakistan State of Future Index (PK-SOFI) to measure where the country stood against its own long-range indicators. I have sat in rooms with the National Intelligence Council, the OECD, the UK Cabinet Office’s Horizon Scanning unit, and South Korea’s Parliamentary Caucus on Foresight, watching how seriously other systems take the discipline of anticipation. And I keep coming back to Pakistan with the same question: why does foresight refuse to take root here, no matter how many divisions we build, how many scenarios we run, or how many white papers we write? The honest answer is not that Pakistan lacks talent or awareness. It is that foresight is not something Pakistan does in public policy. It is not a step in how a budget is drafted, a plan is approved, or a ministry decides what to prioritise. There is no standing government body mandated to scan horizons, run scenarios, and feed the results into policy on a continuing basis. What exists instead is a series of one-off exercises, personality-driven units, and donor-funded pilots that surface, produce a report, and disappear without ever touching an actual decision. We are organised for emergencies, not trajectories. Pakistan has taken 25 IMF bailouts since 1958, meaning a state agency has spent a meaningful share of nearly every decade since Independence negotiating short-term fiscal survival rather than long-term fiscal design. Layer onto that a security environment that has run hot almost continuously (three wars with India, the loss of East Pakistan in 1971, a three-decade counterinsurgency, a live conflict on the western border), floods on a roughly generational cycle, most recently in 2010 and 2022, and governments that rarely complete a full term. Together, these have made firefighting the default posture, not because officials lack the capacity to think ahead, but because the in-tray never empties long enough to look past it. Foresight rewards sitting with uncertainty long enough to map plausible futures before committing to one. In a system permanently in triage, that patience reads as indulgence. Foresight exercises are compressed into single-scenario “national vision” documents because nobody upstream had the appetite for ambiguity. The tool survives; the method dies. Bureaucratic incentives punish the very posture foresight requires. To do this work honestly, you have to say, “here are four ways this could go” instead of, “here is the plan.” Elsewhere, that kind of honesty signals rigour. Here, it reads as weakness. A civil servant who hedges looks unsure of themself in a system that promotes certainty, even manufactured certainty. So departments flatten their outputs into single forecasts dressed up as inevitabilities, because that is what survives a briefing. Devolution without capacity is devolution in name only. After the 18th Amendment, the provinces formally inherited planning authority that used to sit with the Centre. But there is no actual infrastructure of foresight in Pakistan to devolve: no standing data systems, no trained analyst cadre, no dedicated budget lines, no institutional continuity anywhere in the federation. Devolution handed provinces a mandate without a matching capability, because the capability was never built centrally either. I see this starkly in how differently Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and Balochistan engage with long-range planning, and how peripheral AJK and Gilgit-Baltistan remain from almost non-existent national foresight conversations altogether. Institutional memory resets with every change of government. Foresight is cumulative; its value compounds the longer a system tracks its own indicators and holds itself accountable to earlier projections. Pakistan’s governance cycle does not allow for that. Between civilian transitions, military oversight periods, and constant cabinet reshuffling, every vision-focused initiative I have watched get built has been tied to a specific champion rather than a standing function. When that person moves on, the initiative is orphaned. I have seen strategy divisions quietly stop meeting within eighteen months of a leadership change, not because anyone canceled them, but because nobody remembered to keep them alive. Other systems show it can be done differently. Singapore’s Centre for Strategic Futures sits inside the Prime Minister’s Office, government-budgeted, training civil servants across ministries. Finland’s Committee for the Future has sat inside Parliament since the early 1990s and became a permanent standing committee in 2000; by law, every government must present its view of the country’s long-term future, giving foresight a fixed calendar slot regardless of who is in power. The UK runs a standing Horizon Scanning Programme feeding Cabinet-level planning; South Korea’s National Assembly has its own futures institute; the UAE folded foresight into a cabinet-level portfolio in 2016; Wales created a statutory Future Generations Commissioner in 2015 with legal power over public bodies. Even China and the US, opposite in ideology, share the discipline: China’s Five-Year Plans, coordinated by the National Development and Reform Commission since 1953, form a standing apparatus surviving every leadership transition, while the US National Intelligence Council has delivered its Global Trends report to every incoming administration since 1997, produced by a standing unit rather than a sympathetic official’s pet project. None of these systems runs on champions or grant cycles. They run on statute, budget, and a permanent seat inside government, which is exactly the combination Pakistan has never assembled. What ties all of this together, through a systems lens, is a single pathology: Pakistan’s governance architecture has almost none of the feedback loops that let a system self-organise around long-term signals. Self-organising systems need memory, actors with a stake in outcomes beyond their own tenure, and a mechanism that rewards anticipation over reaction. We have built none of those into the state’s core operating logic. So foresight keeps arriving from the outside, as a consultancy, a donor project, a personal initiative, and keeps failing to fuse with the host, the way a graft fails when the underlying tissue can’t support it. An institutionalised foresight function would not eliminate the crises that keep Pakistan in triage; floods, currency shocks, and security shocks are not going away. What it would change is the state’s posture going into them. An IMF program negotiated against standing 10-year fiscal scenarios looks different from one negotiated cycle to cycle, with each finance ministry relearning lessons the last already paid for. A flood response planned against decade-tracked climate projections looks different from one improvised after the water reaches the villages, as in 2010 and 2022. A federation with shared foresight infrastructure would let all six administrative units argue about the future on the same data and time horizon, instead of improvising six separate responses to the same pressures. And a state whose institutional memory did not reset with every government could finally hold itself accountable to its own past projections, the only way this work compounds instead of restarting from zero. None of that requires inventing something new; it requires borrowing the discipline that Singapore, Finland, the UAE, Wales, China, and the United States have each built, and giving foresight the one thing it has never had here: a fixed, funded, legally protected place inside how decisions actually get made. Until then, Pakistan will remain a country that occasionally produces foresight but never practices it as policy: excellent forecasts, run by dedicated individuals, inside departments with no legal footing and no guaranteed tomorrow, that no ministry is obligated to read and no budget is obligated to reflect.

items.title: Police confirm recovery of 9 dead bodies in Niger community
items.description: The Police Command in Niger has confirmed the recovery of nine dead bodies on the Wawa-Lumma road in Borgu Local Government Area of Niger. The victims were suspected to have been killed by bandits while travelling on the road. The Spokesperson for the Niger Police Command, SP Wasiu Abiodun, told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Wednesday in Minna that a team of police and military was dispatched and evacuated the bodies after information was received on Tuesday. He said clearance operations had been intensified with a view to securing the area from any security threat. “Police and military tactical teams were mobilised to the scene; the bodies recovered, while clearance operation was intensified to secure the area,” he said.
