items.title: Republic Bank targets affordable home ownership through JoyNews Habitat Fair
items.description: Republic Bank Ghana is positioning the JoyNews Habitat Fair as a platform to expand access to mortgage financing and help more Ghanaians navigate the path to home ownership, particularly low- and middle-income earners. The bank, which is the title sponsor of the JoyNews Habitat Fair, says it has structured mortgage products to support customers across different income levels. Manager in Charge of Mortgage at Republic Bank, Frank Oppong Yeboah, says the bank’s offerings are designed to make home ownership possible even for people who cannot immediately afford a completed house. “Republic Bank has structured a package for all income levels to help them acquire their property, low, middle and high income. If you have a relationship with Republic Bank, you should be able to acquire your own house if not immediately, over time.” Mr Oppong Yeboah says earners of about GH¢3,000 can explore mortgage financing to first acquire land and subsequently access construction financing after reducing their loan balance. “If you earn GH¢3,000, that amount may not be able to give you enough to buy a house. So what you do is that we have a mortgage that can qualify you to buy land. When you have reduced your balance significantly, we will give you another loan to purchase construction loan to start the construction of the house.” He says the bank’s collaboration with government also offers a mortgage rate of about 8.5 percent, targeted particularly at lower-income earners. “We are working on an interest rate of about 8.5 percent, a single-digit interest rate, in collaboration with the Government of Ghana. If somebody has GH¢3,000, you can qualify as much as GH¢170,000.” The bank is also encouraging prospective homeowners to adopt incremental construction, allowing them to start with what they can afford and expand as their incomes grow. “The incremental development is to help you build without stress, building with your resources. You cut your coat according to your size, and then you get something for yourself and your family. That’s where you begin.” Mr Oppong Yeboah says the bank’s mortgage structure also gives borrowers repayment certainty, with the interest rate remaining unchanged once the facility is booked. “When the mortgage is booked, your interest rate remains the same. When you rent a property, first year you pay your rent. That one-year advance, if you were paying GH¢1,000, would be GH¢12,000. That, if you went a little bit, could have been enough, but you pay the one year to the landlord and at the end of the year, that money is gone,” he said. Republic Bank says its participation in the JoyNews Habitat Fair will provide an opportunity for prospective homeowners to engage directly with the bank on mortgage options, financing requirements and practical pathways to acquiring or building a home. The fair is expected to bring together key players in the housing and property sector to connect prospective homeowners with financing, housing solutions and other services needed to make home ownership more accessible.

items.title: 3 cops arrested for alleged role in prisoner’s escape in Rawalpindi
items.description: RAWALPINDI: Rawalpindi police said on Wednesday that they had arrested three cops, who were posted as guards at Adiala jail, for their alleged involvement in the escape of a prisoner while he was being transported to Jhelum jail from a court in the garrison city. According to a police statement, Assistant Sub-Inspector Tauqeer Hussain, Head Constable Mahboob Khan and Constable Qasim were arrested on the directives of Rawalpindi City Police Officer Hassan Mushtaq Sukhera. Police said the escape took place in the Mandra area on Tuesday, identifying the prisoner as Hammad, who had a record of involvement in cases of “serious crime”. According to police, search operations and raids were underway to arrest the prisoner. According to the first information report, a copy of which is available with Dawn , the prisoner was being transported back to Jhelum jail after a court appearance when the three cops “conspired” with him and made the van driver stop at a hotel along the GT Road near Mandra police station as part of their “escape plan”. The prisoner and the policemen got out at the hotel, where they were joined by three of his accomplices. According to the FIR, the prisoner and his accomplices had planned to escape in a car. However, the police van driver alerted the Mandra police, who reached the spot as the prisoner was attempting to escape. “When the police signalled the accused to stop, Hammad and his accomplices began firing at the police,” the FIR read. It was registered on behalf of the state by Mandra police Station House Officer (SHO) Zakaa ul Hassan. It invoked Sections 324 (attempt to murder), 353 (assault or criminal force to deter a public servant from the discharge of his duty), 186 (obstructing public servant in discharge of public functions), 120-B (punishment for criminal conspiracy), 222 (intentional omission to apprehend on the part of a public servant bound to apprehend a person under sentence or lawfully committed), 223 (escape from confinement or custody negligently suffered by a public servant), 224 (resistance or obstruction by a person to his lawful apprehension), 34 (acts done by several persons in furtherance of a common intention), 118 (concealing design to commit offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life), 440 (mischief committed after preparation made causing death or hurt) of the Pakistan Penal Code, Sections 155-C and 155-D of Police Order 2002, which pertain to misconduct by police officers, and multiple sections of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997. Gujjar Khan Sub-Divisional Police Officer (SDPO) Syed Danyial Hassan told Dawn that Mandra police had managed to arrest one of the accomplices, identified as Danial, and recover an AK-47 from his possession, while the others managed to escape. The official said the police van had also been taken into custody. He told Dawn that the prisoner was accused of killing an Adiala jail official and had been transferred to Jhelum jail a few days ago following the recovery of a mobile phone from his possession at Adiala. In June, 14 under-trial prisoners escaped from a prisoner van while being transported from Kahuta to Adiala jail after overpowering security guards. Four of the escaped prisoners were re-arrested during an operation, a Rawalpindi spokesperson said soon after the incident. The incident occurred within the jurisdiction of Sihala police station in Islamabad district.

items.title: Climate change education must move beyond theory – GAYO Eco-clubs Africa
items.description: Operations and Programs Officer of GAYO Eco-clubs Africa, Patrick AbbeyQuaye, has said climate change education must go beyond classroom discussions and focus more on practical activities that enable young people to understand and respond to environmental challenges. Speaking at WaterAid and JoyNews National Dialogue, Mr AbbeyQuaye said there was still a worrying gap in climate change awareness among young people, including students at the tertiary level. Reflecting on an awareness exercise he participated in at the University of Ghana, he said only a small number of students demonstrated an understanding of climate change. “Out of like 10 people that you meet or had the conversation with, it was only about two people that knew about climate change, and that was because of the courses they were doing,” he said on Wednesday, August 12. He said the situation was particularly concerning because the exercise involved university students who were expected to have greater exposure to environmental issues. Mr AbbeyQuaye said his own understanding of climate change deepened when he studied Marine and Fisheries Science at university, after first encountering the subject through a climate-focused club at the senior high school level. He welcomed efforts by the Ghana Education Service to integrate climate science into the education system but stressed the need for practical learning. “I’m more interested in the practicality of it. Hard education, you don’t do much of the talking. You go to the field,” he said. He urged schools to involve children in simple environmental projects that demonstrate how they can contribute to solving climate-related challenges. According to him, activities such as building simple water filtration systems, waste segregation and basic energy projects could help children develop problem-solving skills and environmental awareness from an early age. He said practical activities could also encourage curiosity among children and inspire them to think about solutions to environmental problems within their communities. Mr AbbeyQuaye acknowledged that some efforts were already being made but said much more needed to be done to ensure climate education translated into action. “I think that it’s still not enough. A lot of effort still needs to be put into it,” he said. He called for more climate-related competitions and practical programmes in schools to complement existing sanitation and environmental initiatives.

items.title: Iranian photojournalist faces 15 years in prison over images, reporting
items.description: Acclaimed Iranian photojournalist Yalda Moaiery has spent much of her career documenting moments of dissent and the lives of women in Iran. The work has repeatedly brought her into conflict ​with the authorities, and on Iran’s National Journalist Day on Saturday she learned she had been sentenced to 15 years in prison. The sentence ‌was handed down under a law enacted after a 12-day war between Israel and Iran in 2025, legislation that Iranian authorities say is intended to combat espionage and cooperation with hostile states. When Moaiery arrived at Tehran’s Revolutionary Court, she was not given formal case documents, she said. Instead, a friend accompanying her copied details from a charge sheet by hand. Rights groups say such ​procedures reflect a lack of transparency in Iran’s judicial system. According to the handwritten notes reviewed by Reuters, the accusations against her include giving interviews to ​media outlets deemed hostile by the authorities and providing photographs to organisations linked to the U.S. and Israel. Reuters could ⁠not independently verify the contents of the charge sheet. In a statement provided to Reuters, Moaiery said the intelligence wing of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps raided her ​home during anti-government protests in January and confiscated her phone, laptop and other electronic equipment. She said IRGC officers returned after the U.S. launched air strikes on Iran ​this year and again seized her belongings. “On this occasion, they took everything, including even the cameras I had owned since childhood,” she said. “I was subjected to several interrogations, and eventually my case was referred to Branch 33 of the Security Prosecutor’s Office and subsequently to the Revolutionary Court.” The spokesman for Iran’s United Nations Mission in New York did not respond to a request ​for comment on her case. Roya Boroumand, executive director of the U.S.-based Abdorrahman Boroumand Center for Human Rights in Iran, said that withholding case documents is an ​effort by the Islamic Republic to “silence” defendants and showed the judiciary “blatantly” acting as a state agent. A CAREER CHRONICLING WOMEN’S LIVES IN IRAN The handwritten document provided by Moaiery to Reuters lists accusations ‌including “interviewing with ⁠networks hostile to the system” and sending photographs to entities in the United States and Israel that it describes as “hostile”. Moaiery said she shared photographs showing damage from air strikes in Iran with CNN and appeared in an interview about her reporting, in March 2026. She has 10 days to appeal under the 2025 espionage law, half the time allowed under previous legislation. Moaiery has previously been imprisoned for her work. She served two years in Gharchak Prison, a place that she had previously photographed. In 2022, she ​spent three months in jail and was ​sentenced to eight years in prison ⁠for covering the nationwide “Woman, Life, Freedom” uprisings that erupted after the death of young Iranian woman Mahsa Amini in police custody. An amnesty later reduced the sentence, but she said the case continued to expose her to questioning by authorities. Reporters Without ​Borders, says 16 journalists have been detained in Iran this year. Moaiery’s work has mainly focused on women. She photographed some ​of the earliest documented ⁠detentions of women by morality police, including a 2007 image showing two women sitting in white police vans, with tears streaming down their faces. In 2017, she photographed a student protesting at economic conditions at Tehran University. The woman walks through tear gas, raising her fist in the air. The image was used by the Trump administration in its comments ⁠on human ​rights in Iran. Moaiery said she remained committed to her work despite the prospect of further imprisonment. “None ​of these sentences, however, has ever caused me to abandon my path, even for a moment. I have continued to document and show the realities of Iranian society,” she said. “I don’t have anything to ​lose. The regime took everything from me and the only thing that I still have is my truth and honesty as an observer.”

items.title: Burkina/Coupures nocturnes d'électricité : La SONABEL apporte des éclaircissements
items.description: ‎Les coupures d'électricité enregistrées ces dernières semaines durant la nuit dans plusieurs villes du Burkina s'expliquent par un phénomène naturel saisonnier. Dans une note d'information publiée le 11 août 2026 sur sa page Facebook, la Société nationale d'électricité du Burkina (SONABEL) a indiqué que les perturbations constatées dans les régions du Nazinon, du Djôrô, du Yaadga et du Nando sont principalement liées à la migration massive de chauves-souris frugivores, communément appelées roussettes. ‎ ‎La SONABEL explique que ces mammifères volants se déplacent en grands essaims pendant la nuit, notamment entre 20 heures et 5 heures du matin. Au cours de leurs déplacements, ils entrent fréquemment en contact avec les lignes électriques moyenne tension, provoquant des courts-circuits à l'origine des interruptions temporaires de la fourniture d'électricité. ‎ ‎Face à cette situation, la SONABEL assure que ses équipes d'intervention restent mobilisées et en état d'alerte permanente. Des patrouilles sont régulièrement déployées afin d'identifier les zones touchées, procéder aux réparations nécessaires et rétablir le courant dans les meilleurs délais. La SONABEL précise également que ses services techniques travaillent activement à la mise en œuvre de solutions durables pour limiter l'impact de ce phénomène environnemental récurrent sur le réseau électrique. ‎ ‎Tout en présentant ses excuses aux abonnés pour les désagréments occasionnés, la SONABEL souligne que ces perturbations sont indépendantes de sa volonté et remercie les usagers pour leur compréhension et leur confiance. Pour tout signalement d'anomalie ou demande d'information, les abonnés peuvent contacter le Centre d'appels de la SONABEL au 80 00 11 30. ‎ ‎Lefaso.net ‎Source : Page Facebook SONABEL

items.title: Eclipse solaire partielle dans le ciel des 5 pays arabes dont la Mauritanie
items.description: Certaines régions de la Mauritanie, de la Libye, de l'Algérie, du Maroc et de la Tunisie observent ce mercredi une éclipse solaire partielle, parallèlement à l'éclipse totale qui traverse certaines zones du Groenland, de l'Islande, de l'Espagne et du nord de la Russie, selon les données de la NASA. La Mauritanie connaîtra une éclipse partielle, avec un pourcentage d’occultation inférieur à celui de l’Algérie, du Maroc et de la Tunisie ; le degré d’occultation du disque solaire, ainsi que l’heure du début et du pic de l’éclipse, varient d’un pays à l’autre. Certaines régions d’Afrique du Nord-Ouest connaîtront des taux d’occultation élevés, tandis que le phénomène restera partiel dans les pays arabes, dont aucun ne se trouve sur la trajectoire de l’éclipse totale. Une éclipse solaire se produit lorsque la lune passe entre la Terre et le Soleil, masquant ainsi une partie de la lumière solaire sur certaines zones de la surface terrestre. Dans les régions situées en dehors de la bande de l’éclipse totale, on observe la Lune masquant uniquement une partie du disque solaire. La NASA souligne qu’il est dangereux de regarder directement le Soleil pendant les phases de l’éclipse partielle, même lorsque la partie masquée du disque solaire est importante. Il est indispensable d’utiliser des lunettes spéciales pour observer l’éclipse ou des dispositifs d’observation solaire sécurisés afin de protéger les yeux.

items.title: Tata Group Chairman N Chandrasekaran to step down in February
items.description: N Chandrasekaran, the chairman of Tata Group, has said that he will not seek reappointment when his term ends in February. The 63-year-old said the decision came after the board of Tata Sons could not reach a resolution on a five-year extension of his term, months after the proposal first came up. The news sent shares of listed Tata companies plunging and has led to questions over what lies ahead for the gigantic salt-to-steel conglomerate that owns Air India, Tata Steel and Jaguar Land Rover. Chandrasekaran’s resignation, which comes days ahead of Tata Sons’ annual general meeting, points to tensions that have been playing out for months after a boardroom power battle erupted between trustees. The Tata Group is uniquely structured – a charitable arm called Tata Trusts owns 66% of the group’s parent company, Tata Sons. This has given the group tax and regulatory advantages, and allows it to carry out charitable activities, but experts say that its dual non-profit and commercial objectives have sometimes led to governance issues. Tata Trusts has three nominees on the Tata Sons board. Reports have said that the board members have disagreed over issues such as board nominations, funding approvals and the public listing of Tata Sons. The group has not publicly commented on the discord. The internal rifts threatened to distract the group while it was facing severe business headwinds including the revival of Air India, which it bought from the Indian government in 2022. When the proposal for his extension was brought before the board in February, one board member did not support it, Chandrasekaran said in his statement without naming the person. “In the absence of unanimous support, I chose to defer the decision,” he said, adding that there was no resolution even six months later. “Tata Sons is a very large institution and there are many strategic projects that are under critical stages of execution. It is not only necessary to have a leader in place to lead the Group beyond Feb 2027, but also clarity on leadership is important for employees, investors, partners and other stakeholders,” he said. Chandrasekaran was named the group’s chairman in 2017. He replaced the late Cyrus Mistry, whose abrupt removal from the post months earlier had triggered a bitter legal battle. Before becoming chairman, Chandrasekaran was the CEO and managing director of the group’s high-profile global IT service provider, Tata Consultancy Services. He joined the group in 1987 – a 2017 press release announcing his appointment as chairman described him as a “Tata lifer”. Ambareesh Baliga, an independent market analyst, said that when a person with Chandrasekaran’s stature stepped down like this, it was inevitable that the markets would react negatively. “However, they have six months to find a good successor,” he said, adding that he thought it likely that the next leader would be chosen from within the group.

items.title: Private sector credit grows 41.2%; BoG governor urges banks to deepen lending
items.description: Private sector credit in Ghana grew by 41.2% in June 2026, a significant increase from the 8.6% recorded in the same period last year, as easing financial conditions begin to translate into stronger lending to businesses. Governor of the Bank of Ghana (BoG), Dr. Johnson Asiama, disclosed the development when he engaged Chief Executive Officers and heads of banks, noting that real private sector credit growth also stood at 34.1%. “Financial conditions have eased significantly. In the money market, interest rates have continued to moderate across various market segments. These developments are beginning to translate into stronger credit flows to the private sector,” Dr. Asiama said. He described the growth in private sector credit as “a significant development,” against the backdrop of declining inflation and relatively stable financial conditions. The Governor said the improving economic environment presents an opportunity for banks to play a stronger role in supporting economic activity, particularly by expanding access to finance for businesses. However, he noted that despite the rebound in credit creation and growing demand for loans, many small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), particularly those operating along the agricultural value chain, continue to face difficulties accessing financing. “Many SMEs, particularly those on the agricultural value chain, still struggle to access finance, just because banks continue to perceive these businesses as relatively high risk,” he said. Dr. Asiama therefore urged banks to deepen their understanding of the businesses and sectors they serve and develop innovative and flexible credit products that better reflect the realities of borrowers. He specifically called for loan repayment structures that take into account the seasonal nature of agricultural activities and the timing of borrowers’ cash flows. “This should include developing innovative and flexible credit products that recognise the seasonal nature of agricultural activities and align loan repayment schedules with the timing and pattern of borrowers’ cash flows,” the Governor said. He stressed that banks should see themselves not merely as financial intermediaries but as partners in the growth and transformation of the Ghanaian economy. “As banks, you are not merely financial intermediaries, you are important business partners in the growth and transformation of the economy,” Dr. Asiama stated. The latest credit growth comes as Ghana’s broader macroeconomic conditions continue to improve. Real GDP growth reached 6.4% in the first quarter of 2026, while headline inflation declined to 4.6% in July from 5.3% in June. The Monetary Policy Committee has maintained the policy rate at 14%, with the Bank saying the current stance remains appropriate as it assesses the evolving economic and geopolitical environment. Meanwhile, developments within the banking sector also point to improved resilience. Total banking sector assets increased by 30.7% in June 2026, while the industry’s capital adequacy ratio rose to 20.4%, from 10.6% a year earlier. The non-performing loan ratio also declined to 16.1% in June 2026, from 23.1% over the same period last year. Dr. Asiama said these developments provide a stronger foundation for banks to support businesses and households and contribute to sustainable economic growth. The Governor’s comments come at a time when the Bank of Ghana is seeking to ensure that the improvement in macroeconomic stability translates into increased economic activity and broader access to finance.

items.title: Arewa Youths laud Tinubu over creation of 10 division in Taraba
items.description: By Femi Bolaji JALINGO — Youths under the aegis of the Arewa Youth Assembly on Wednesday staged a rally in Jalingo, the Taraba State capital, to commend President Bola Tinubu for the establishment of the 10 Division of the Nigerian Army in the state. Addressing journalists during the procession, the spokesperson for the group, Aliyu Mohammad Sani, described the development as a strategic intervention that would strengthen security operations in Taraba and the wider North-East region. Sani said the establishment of the division demonstrated the Federal Government’s commitment to addressing security concerns affecting communities in the region. He said, “This division is a fortress for Taraba and a shield for the entire North-East. For too long, our communities cried out for a force that understood our landscape, our fears and our hopes, and Mr President answered that call.” He also commended the Federal Government for the recent increase in the salaries of military personnel, describing it as a morale booster for troops serving in frontline areas. “It tells every man and woman on the front line that their sacrifice is seen and their blood is honoured,” he said. Sani also commended the Chief of Defence Staff and the Chief of Army Staff for their efforts toward strengthening the country’s security architecture. He said the establishment of the division had given residents renewed confidence in ongoing efforts to address insecurity. Also speaking, the spokesperson for the Taraba People’s Movement, Comrade Umar Sani Bello, said the solidarity march was organised to convey the appreciation of residents to the Federal Government for the establishment of the military formation. Bello said the development had renewed hope for improved security in the region, adding that the people of Taraba were ready to collaborate with the Nigerian Army and other security agencies to enhance security operations in the state. The post Arewa Youths laud Tinubu over creation of 10 division in Taraba appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: New attacks on shipping as Iran war talks hit fresh impasse
items.description: The U.S. and Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis reported separate attacks on shipping on Tuesday as prospects for ending the Iran war appeared to dim, with Tehran saying the Strait of ​Hormuz would remain closed unless Washington accepts its conditions. The attacks, in the Gulf of Oman leading to the strait and at the entrance to the Red Sea — both vital chokepoints ‌for global oil supplies — come as the war shows no signs of ending despite repeated assertions from U.S. President Donald Trump of a deal being imminent. Oil prices gained and global shares retreated amid renewed pessimism about a quick end to the conflict. Brent crude futures climbed 1.4% to settle at $88.91 per barrel and U.S. crude rose 1.3% to $83.20. At the southern end of the Red Sea, four crew members were killed in a suspected Houthi attack on a small cargo vessel in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on Tuesday, Yemen’s Transport ​Ministry said. Two Yemeni rescuers from an anti-Houthi military group were also killed, Yemen’s Coast Guard said. The fatalities aboard the Egyptian-owned Tihamah, if confirmed, would be the first deaths on shipping by Yemen’s ​Iran-aligned Houthis since the Iran war began. The Houthi-run news agency Saba reported that the group, which said last month it would impose a naval blockade on Saudi ⁠Arabia in the Red Sea, attacked a Saudi ship they said was carrying military equipment in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. It did not name the ship, and there was no immediate Saudi response to the report. The U.S. military, ​meanwhile, said a U.S. Navy MH-60 helicopter fired two Hellfire missiles to disable the steering gear of a Panama-flagged cargo ship. The ship ignored repeated warnings to stop violating a naval blockade on Iranian ports, the U.S. Central Command said. ​Maritime sources told Reuters the ship was hit off Pakistan while sailing into the Gulf of Oman. STEPPED UP RHETORIC Both Iran and the United States have stepped up rhetoric in the past two days. Iran’s top security official, Mohsen Rezaei, said on Tuesday that the vital Strait of Hormuz shipping route will remain closed unless the U.S. accepts Iran’s conditions to end the war – the release of Iran’s frozen assets and an end to conflicts throughout the region, including in Lebanon and Gaza. That followed a new demand from Trump ​on Monday that Iran should pay compensation for people killed in 50 years of wars, attacks and protests. Throughout the conflict, Trump has alternated between threats of escalation and claims that a peace deal is imminent. In an interview ​released late on Monday, he suggested the uncertainty could last for a while, saying he might just “bop along” and let Tehran fail economically, or hit them “really, really hard.” “I’m sort of negotiating,” Trump told Real America’s Voice. “They’re very devious negotiators.” Speaking to ‌reporters after a ⁠visit to Ohio on Tuesday, Trump said “Iran is going fine, going just absolutely fine.” “We totally control the Strait of Hormuz … Nobody else, only us,” he said. “At some point, maybe they’ll do something and then they get blown away,” he said of Iran. “But right now, we’re in a very good position. We have a country that has been the bully of the Middle East for 50 years, really 51 if you think about it … and they’re no longer the bully of the Middle East.” Asked about an incident in which he switched planes in Turkey last month because of worries over reports of a potential Iranian assassination threat, Trump suggested the alternative aircraft may have ​faced greater risk. “That would be the plane I think ​that they would be more likely to go ⁠for,” he told reporters after The Washington Post broke the story about him secretly taking a military flight instead of Air Force One in an operation involving him being moved between aircraft in a catering truck. “Any consequential president has a lot of threats,” Trump added. “I don’t worry about anything.” The comments from Rezaei, appointed on Sunday ​as second-in-command of the body that coordinates Iran’s security and foreign policy, were the strongest indication the Strait of Hormuz would not reopen to shipping anytime ​soon. The waterway handled a fifth ⁠of global oil and liquefied natural gas flow before the war. “As long as America does not change its behaviour and does not accept Iran’s conditions, the Strait of Hormuz will not be opened,” Rezaei said, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency. There was no immediate comment from Washington on Iran’s latest comments. Thousands of people have been killed in the conflict since the U.S. and Israel launched attacks on Iran on February 28. Iran has struck U.S. assets and infrastructure in ⁠countries including Oman, ​Jordan, Kuwait, Israel, the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia. Raising the prospect of further escalation, Mohammad Reza Naqdi, an adviser to the ​commander of Iran’s Revolutionary Guards, said on Iranian state TV on Tuesday that the corps was developing the ability to carry out operations “on enemy soil.” “We need to be able to move the operations to the enemy’s soil, whenever this is needed and ordered,” he said. “This ​is the characteristic of the offensive doctrine that has to be attained.”

items.title: Israeli settlers besieging Palestinian families in West Bank village
items.description: Israeli settlers have been besieging two Palestinian families in their homes in the occupied West Bank since Sunday, with the families saying their supplies were running out and rights groups urging the authorities to step in. On Wednesday Israeli security forces were reported to have withdrawn from the Jewish settler outpost in the village of Qusra near Nablus, following clashes with a crowd of extremist settlers. About a dozen settlers are said to remain at the site. After the Palestinian homeowners made their initial report to the Israeli army, the first soldiers who arrived at the scene were filmed praying with the settlers. The Abu Ridi and Hassan families have been posting on social media appealing for help after their water and power supplies were cut off and their food stocks ran low. The latest developments come as a top UN official told the Security Council in New York on Tuesday that “the West Bank is at breaking point”. All settlements are illegal under international law. Outposts are set up without official Israeli authorisation. Palestinian security camera footage shows settlers tearing down a wall outside the Abu Ridi family’s home on Sunday evening and using the stones to block the road. This left seven people – including two young girls – unable to leave their homes while other Palestinians could not reach them. They live in what is known as Area B, part of the West Bank under Palestinian administrative control and Israeli security control. Posting on Facebook, Qusay Abu Ridi said the situation was critical, “especially as we are completely isolated.” He wrote: “We are living in our own home, on our own land, and we are asking for nothing more than the right to live safely and with dignity.” On Monday, Israeli settlers blocked Israeli journalists from the left-leaning Haaretz newspaper from trying to reach the Palestinian properties. The reporters said Israeli soldiers at the scene refused to help them when their car was blocked for two hours. They were told the area was a closed military zone, however the order was not enforced on the settlers. A day later the Israeli human rights group Yesh Din urgently appealed to the head of the Israeli military’s Central Command for the army to protect the besieged residents, evacuate the settlers’ outpost and hold the settlers accountable. Late on Tuesday, a Palestinian ambulance was finally allowed to reach the families, delivering food and taking one child away for medical treatment. At about the same time, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) put out a statement condemning the establishment of the new outpost. It said that entering and seizing Palestinian homes was “illegal, reprehensible, and unacceptable activity”. When the head of its Central Command, Maj Gen Avi Bluth and other senior officers arrived at the scene early on Wednesday they are said to have met residents and voiced their “grave concern”. Afterwards, Palestinian security camera video shared with the BBC showed confrontations between Israeli soldiers and border police and a large crowd of settlers. The security forces used tear gas and stun grenades. In other footage, the Israeli forces appear to have confiscated the canopy under which the settlers were sheltering, while leaving their other equipment. “Border Police forces evacuated the tent and are working to evacuate the civilians who were staying there. The incident is still ongoing,” the IDF stated. It said it was decided that “disciplinary action would be taken against the security personnel involved, who were documented at the site several days ago”. The Palestinian village mayor, Abdel Azim Wadi, told the BBC that local residents had seen “a clear and sustained pattern of targeting Qusra”. Last month a newly completed mosque was set on fire with graffiti in Hebrew sprayed nearby. That settler attack was one of many that followed on from an incident in the Palestinian village of Tal. After Israeli settlers attacked Tal, it triggered an escalation in which six people were killed – four Palestinians and two Israeli soldiers – one of whom acted as a security coordinator for a nearby Israeli settlement. In July, settlers also surrounded a Palestinian home in the village of Jalud, near Qusra, for more than two weeks. Afterwards, the owners fled and settlers took over the property where they remain until now. “Settler violence has reached unprecedented levels,” the UN’s Deputy Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process, Ramiz Alakbarov, told the Security Council in a briefing on Tuesday. He gave what he described as “the sobering human toll” and mentioned that the Nablus Governorate in particular had been hit hard recently by violence. According to the UN’s figures, 76 Palestinians – including 18 children – have been killed in the West Bank this year, by Israeli forces or settlers. At the same time, three Israelis – including one civilian – were killed in confrontations with Palestinians and in an alleged ramming attack by a Palestinian in the West Bank. Since January 2023, 127 Palestinian communities in the West Bank have experienced full or partial displacement, including 47 that have been entirely displaced, affecting more than 6,390 Palestinians, the UN says. It has registered that in 2026, about 3,800 Palestinians, nearly half of them children, have been displaced due to settler violence, demolitions and evictions. Speaking at the UN meeting, Israel’s Ambassador to the UN, Danny Danon dismissed the idea that settlements were an obstacle to peace. He said that they would remain and continue to grow as his country had biblical, historic and legal rights to the land. He said that the Security Council “must understand a simple truth: we are not going anywhere.”

items.title: Zhu Rongji, who helped turn China into a trading giant, dies at 97
items.description: Former Chinese Premier Zhu Rongji, who spearheaded China’s entry into global trade and laid the foundation for its explosive growth, has died at the age of 97. He served in the country’s second-highest office from 1998-2003 and played a leading role in securing its entry into the World Trade Organization, opening Chinese factories to the international market and drawing foreign investment. He was one of the most important economic reformers who moved local tax powers to the central government, closed or privatised failing state firms and promoted home ownership. Many in China remember him as a tough and pragmatic leader who delivered double-digit growth and wa rarely afraid to speak his mind. In 1998, he said China was facing “many potential crises that could erupt at any time… “Ordinary people are discontent about us in many ways. Especially, there is corruption among officials, the gulf between rich and poor and the way some local officials act like tyrants.” He labelled rogue bankers as “half-wits” and said the dams and flood dykes lining the Yangtze River were as “flimsy and porous as tofu dregs”. Under his leadership, which helped stabilise the economy and tackle corruption, China began transforming into a manufacturing powerhouse, leaving behind its status as a Communist outsider. Though he faced criticism because those reforms also led to 30 million lay-offs over five years, and with huge growth came more inequality. Chinese state media describe Zhu Rongji’s life as one of “revolution, struggle and brilliance”. He was born in the central province of Hunan in 1928 and earned a degree in electrical engineering before joining the civil service. He joined the Communist Party in 1949, but was purged twice – first after criticising Mao Zedong’s economic policies as “irrational” and being labelled a “rightist”, and again during the Cultural Revolution. Zhu was brought back into the fold after Mao’s death, and by 1991 had risen to the role of vice-premier in charge of China’s economy. He took the role of premier seven years later. Zhu led China through difficult negotiations to enter the World Trade Organization in 2002. In state media his obituary described him as an “outstanding member of the Communist Party of China and loyal Commnist fighter… an outstanding leader of the Party and state”.

items.title: Pénurie de cash en Guinée : « nous avons réussi à sécuriser l’approvisionnement en billets » (Karamo Kaba, BCRG)
items.description: Au cours du point de presse animé mardi 11 août 2026 par le gouvernement guinéen pour évoquer la conclusion d’un accord technique avec le Fonds monétaire international (FMI), d’un montant de près de 425 millions de dollars, le gouverneur de la Banque centrale de la République de Guinée (BCRG), Dr Karamo Kaba, a apporté des précisions sur la pénurie de cash qui avait récemment touché le pays. Il a également annoncé des mesures prises pour éviter qu’une telle situation ne se reproduise. Selon le gouverneur de la BCRG, il ne s’agissait pas d’une pénurie de liquidités au sens large, mais d’une difficulté liée à la disponibilité des billets en espèces. « Il y a un an, on parlait beaucoup de pénurie de cash, mais ce n’était pas une pénurie de liquidité. En Guinée, actuellement, tous les paiements effectués par virement, par transaction électronique ou par chèque n’ont jamais connu de pénurie. Il y a eu une pénurie uniquement par rapport au cash. Je veux juste dire que le franc guinéen, il ne se mange qu’en Guinée. Le problème est que nous ne savions pas où étaient ces billets, mais ils n’étaient pas dans les caveaux des banques », a-t-il expliqué. Évoquant les difficultés liées à l’approvisionnement en billets, Dr Karamo Kaba a également rappelé les problèmes rencontrés au niveau du coton, utilisé comme support pour leur fabrication. « Vous savez, c’est le support pour fabriquer les billets. Étant donné qu’il y avait une forte demande d’approvisionnement de plusieurs pays, les imprimeurs avaient des difficultés à satisfaire tout le monde », a-t-il indiqué. Le gouverneur de la BCRG assure toutefois que la situation s’est améliorée grâce aux dispositions prises avec les partenaires. « Aujourd’hui, par rapport à l’offre, nous sommes tout à fait sereins. Nous avons réussi à sécuriser l’approvisionnement en billets », a-t-il annoncé. Plus loin, Dr Karamo Kaba a souligné les efforts engagés pour réduire la dépendance au cash, notamment à travers le développement des paiements électroniques. « Il y a une dizaine de jours, nous avons également lancé NimbaPay pour doper les paiements électroniques. Aujourd’hui, les chiffres de la Banque centrale montrent que les injections de liquidités diminuent chaque semaine, et les banques recommencent à reverser de l’argent, ce qui n’arrivait pas auparavant. La situation est en train de s’améliorer », a-t-il conclu. Elisa CAMARA L’article Pénurie de cash en Guinée : « nous avons réussi à sécuriser l’approvisionnement en billets » (Karamo Kaba, BCRG) est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Pakistan ‘still far’ from becoming a social welfare state: PM Shehbaz
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday said that Pakistan was “still far” from becoming a social welfare state, which he said was the original purpose of the country’s formation. The premier was speaking at an event in Islamabad to mark International Youth Day 2026, observed on August 12. He also inaugurated several initiatives for the youth, including the Power Sector Innovation Programme, the National Youth Employment Policy and the Skills Ambassador Programme. As part of the National Youth Employment Policy, the premier announced that a 35 per cent quota would be specified for women in the labour force. Every year, a 10pc quota will be specified for startups as well to facilitate youth in starting their own businesses, he said. In his speech, PM Shehbaz said that Daanish schools were a step towards making Pakistan a country where young people would have equal opportunities for advancement, irrespective of their financial status. He said that during his tenure as Punjab chief minister, he had established Daanish schools to improve access to quality education for the poor. “How unfortunate is it that, on the one hand, there is a Pakistan for the children of the elite, who not only receive the best education in Pakistan but also attend the best international institutions in the UK and North America? “Contrastingly, there is another Pakistan where millions of parents’ children, who desperately want an education, are not provided even basic educational opportunities.” Today, thousands of graduates of Daanish schools are doctors, engineers and teachers, he said. The PM said that progress being achieved through Daanish schools was a realisation of the dream that Quaid-i-Azam had for Pakistan. Addressing the Daanish school students present in the audience, he said, “the largest part of Pakistan’s population is you. And if we could not give you essential skills, then we won’t be forgiven in this world or the next.” PM Shehbaz mentioned that in this year’s budget, an amount has been specified for youth empowerment and development. Like last year, 1,000 high-achieving students will be sent to China this year for agriculture education, the premier said. He announced that in addition, this year, high-achieving students would be given a state-funded opportunity to study IT and AI in China. He also announced that “Pakistan’s top university” is being established in Pakistan, to be named Daanish University. It would be focused on technology education. Education at Daanish University will be provided free of cost, only based on merit, the premier said. PM Shehbaz added that 250,000 high-achieving students all over Pakistan would be awarded Chromebook laptops this year. He commented that his laptop scheme, when it was first started in Punjab, was criticised but, he added, the programme has allowed the youth to gain advancement opportunities. “Today, I, in front of the youth, promise that until Allah has given me the responsibility to serve the nation, I will do everything in my power for your prosperity and employment. “Our ancestors built Pakistan in 1947, and the Pakistan of 2047 will be built by your vision and energy,” the premier told the students attending the event. Chairman of the Prime Minister’s Youth Programme Rana Mashhood Ahmed Khan also spoke at the event, where he said, “We work day and night for our youth.” He praised PM Shehbaz for providing opportunities for the youth during his tenure as chief minister of Punjab and commended the premier’s leadership in advancing Pakistan, adding that under his leadership, no one could stop the country from moving forward. “The world is talking about Pakistan’s progress today,” he said.

items.title: Tribune libre: Allez en Chine, à la recherche du savoir, mais aussi de l’amitié et du bonheur
items.description: (Tang Zhongdong, Ambassadeur de Chine en Mauritanie) Chers amis mauritaniens, si vous me demandiez de vous présenter la Chine, je pourrais bien sûr vous parler de la Grande Muraille, de la Cité interdite, des pandas, ou encore de cette civilisation vieille de plus de 5 000 ans et dont l’histoire ne s’est jamais interrompue. Mais j’aimerais surtout vous dire que la Chine ne se résume pas à celle que vous voyez dans les livres, à la télévision ou sur les réseaux sociaux. La Chine est vaste et diverse. Vous pouvez la découvrir sous différents angles. Si vous aimez l’histoire et la culture, vous pouvez gravir la Grande Muraille à Beijing, admirer les soldats en terre cuite à Xi’an, ou encore naviguer sur le lac à Hangzhou tout en dégustant du thé chinois. Si vous aimez la nature, vous pouvez contempler les montagnes enneigées du Xizang, admirer les paysages et les lacs du Yunnan, ou découvrir les vastes prairies et les déserts du Xinjiang. Si vous aimez les nouvelles technologies, vous découvrirez une autre facette de la Chine. Vous pourrez prendre le train à grande vitesse, faire l’expérience des robots intelligents, des drones et des véhicules autonomes. Vous pourrez également visiter une usine de véhicules à énergies nouvelles et voir comment une automobile est assemblée à partir de pièces détachées pour devenir un véhicule intelligent. Et si vous en avez l’occasion, vous pourrez même assister de vos propres yeux au lancement d’une fusée. En Chine, l’ancien et le moderne, la tradition et l’innovation n’ont jamais été séparés. Le matin, vous pourrez peut-être boire un bol de lait de soja à côté d’un bâtiment ancien datant de plusieurs siècles. L’après-midi, vous pourrez monter à bord d’un train à grande vitesse roulant à plus de 300 kilomètres à l’heure pour vous rendre d’une ville à une autre. Le soir, vous pourrez commander votre repas avec votre téléphone, prendre le métro ou acheter votre billet de cinéma en quelques clics. Voilà la Chine d’aujourd’hui : une Chine riche d’une histoire millénaire et débordante d’énergie et de vitalité modernes. Aujourd’hui, les jeunes étrangers découvrent la Chine à travers des aspects toujours plus variés. La cuisine chinoise, les séries télévisées chinoises, la culture du thé ainsi que la vie quotidienne des Chinois sont devenues autant de fenêtres permettant de mieux comprendre la Chine. Elles attirent également un nombre croissant de touristes étrangers qui souhaitent venir eux-mêmes à la rencontre de ce pays. Au premier semestre 2026, la Chine a accueilli 22,914 millions d’entrées de ressortissants étrangers, soit une hausse de 20,4 % par rapport à la même période de l’année précédente. Avec la mise en place de mesures visant à faciliter le séjour et les achats des touristes étrangers, notamment le remboursement immédiat de la détaxe à la sortie du territoire, de plus en plus de touristes étrangers, tout en admirant les paysages de la Chine et en découvrant la richesse de sa culture, s’intéressent également à la grande diversité des produits chinois. Drones, lunettes de réalité virtuelle, produits culturels et créatifs, jouets tendance et bien d’autres « nouvelles spécialités chinoises » trouvent désormais leur place dans les valises des visiteurs étrangers. Le « Made in China » n’est depuis longtemps plus seulement synonyme de produits de bon rapport qualité-prix ; il reflète de plus en plus la richesse culturelle de la Chine ainsi que la créativité et l’esprit d’innovation de sa jeune génération. Et lorsque vous viendrez en Chine, vous découvrirez peut-être quelque chose d’intéressant : les Chinois et les Mauritaniens ont en réalité beaucoup de points communs. Nous aimons tous boire du thé, nous aimons tous manger du riz, nous attachons tous une grande importance aux retrouvailles en famille lors des grandes fêtes, et nous sommes tous connus pour notre hospitalité. C’est pour cette raison que je suis convaincu que les échanges entre la Chine et la Mauritanie ne sont pas seulement des échanges entre deux États, mais aussi des échanges entre les peuples, et tout particulièrement entre les jeunes des deux pays. Aujourd’hui, nous vivons dans un monde où l’information est plus connectée que jamais. Grâce aux réseaux sociaux, nous pouvons découvrir en quelques secondes la vie quotidienne à l’autre bout de la planète. Mais je reste convaincu que, même avec la meilleure qualité d’image, la Chine que vous voyez sur un écran ne pourra jamais remplacer l’expérience de venir vous-même en Chine. Alors, chers amis, si vous en avez l’occasion, je vous invite sincèrement à venir en Chine, à la parcourir et à la découvrir. Je suis certain qu’en entrant véritablement au cœur de la Chine, vous ne découvrirez pas seulement un pays qui connaît un développement rapide, mais aussi un pays riche de son histoire, de sa culture, de ses technologies et de son dynamisme, un pays chaleureux, vivant et profondément humain. Dans le monde arabe, un proverbe largement répandu dit : « Cherche le savoir, même s’il se trouve jusqu’en Chine. » Aujourd’hui, j’aimerais reprendre cette ancienne parole pour m’adresser aux jeunes amis mauritaniens : Allez en Chine ! Allez-y à la recherche du savoir, allez-y pour découvrir une Chine authentique et pleine de couleurs, mais aussi pour y trouver l’amitié et le bonheur.

items.title: Centrafrique: l’ambassadeur de France visé par une procédure disciplinaire
items.description: Le diplomate français auprès de la République centrafricaine, Bruno Foucher, est visé par une procédure disciplinaire du Quai d’Orsay, selon des médias, ce mercredi 12 août 2026. De commun accord avec la Centrafrique, le Quai d’Orsay a lancé une procédure disciplinaire visant son diplomate, accusé d’avoir fait venir dans la résidence des jeunes femmes entre janvier 2024 et mars 2026 avec qui il a eu des relations sexuelles avec certaines. Le ministère des Affaires étrangères de la Centrafrique, a confirmé, le mardi 11 août 2026, cette information. Le comportement du diplomate français Bruno Foucher a poussé les services de protection à signaler une faille de sécurité. Une fois alerté, le ministère a procédé à une inspection sur place en avril, qui a entraîné l’ouverture de la procédure disciplinaire. Le mis en cause pourrait subir une sanction disciplinaire pouvant aller du simple blâme à la radiation de la fonction publique en passant par la mise à la retraite d’office. En mars, le ministre français des affaires étrangères Jean-Noël Barrot, en visite à Bangui, avait salué «la restauration complète des relations» entre les deux pays. Il s’agissait de la première visite française de haut niveau en Centrafrique depuis 2018. Par Wakat Séra L’article Centrafrique: l’ambassadeur de France visé par une procédure disciplinaire est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Climate change is worsening water scarcity in the Northern Ghana – Youth Climate Advocate
items.description: Youth Climate Advocate Jerry Anaba Nyaaba has said climate change is worsening water scarcity in northern Ghana, with communities in the Upper East and Upper West regions increasingly struggling to access water for domestic use, schools and healthcare facilities. Speaking at the WaterAid and JoyNews National Dialogue on Wednesday, August 12, Mr Nyaaba said the impact of climate change was becoming increasingly evident in the northern parts of the country, where declining groundwater availability was making it difficult for communities to rely on traditional sources such as wells. He noted that in some areas of the Upper East Region, wells that previously provided water were now failing to yield water even after being dug. “Sometimes when you dig a well this time, you don’t get water. That is telling you something,” he said. According to him, the situation could become more severe in the coming years if urgent measures are not taken to improve water security and build communities’ resilience to climate change. He warned that without intervention, communities could be forced to depend on water transported from other areas to replenish depleted water sources. “This is a very terrible thing. Water scarcity for schools, for health centres, and even for households has become a major problem for the northern communities,” Mr Nyaaba said. He said residents in some communities had to walk several kilometres to access potable water, sometimes spending hours fetching water for basic domestic needs. The situation, he noted, was also affecting education, particularly during the dry season. Mr Nyaaba said students in some senior high schools spend considerable time searching for water instead of preparing for classes. “When you go to most of the senior high schools, from January to somewhere June, students spend much time searching for what to grab before going to class than the time they spend learning,” he said. He added that water shortages were equally affecting health facilities and placing a disproportionate burden on women, who often bear responsibility for fetching water for households and institutions. “Women suffer the most,” he stressed, describing the situation as a current reality rather than a distant threat. Mr Nyaaba is therefore calling for urgent investments in climate-resilient water systems and infrastructure in northern Ghana. He said the country must increase the number of dams and other water storage facilities in the north to help communities cope with prolonged dry periods. “We need climate-resilient water. We need more dams in the north,” he said. He also urged authorities to take advantage of the rainy season to harvest and store water for use during periods of scarcity. “This is the time we have enough water. Can we start harvesting rainwater and be using it in the garden?” he asked. Mr Nyaaba said the situation required coordinated action from government, development partners, communities and other duty bearers to prevent water scarcity from worsening. He warned that failure to address the problem could have serious consequences for the future development and wellbeing of people in northern Ghana.

items.title: Birth registration: NPC, UNICEF unite to give every child legal identity
items.description: By Chioma Obinna & Rotimi Ojomoyela The National Population Commission (NPC), National Identity Management Commission (NIMC), Association of Local Governments of Nigeria (ALGON) and the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) have intensified efforts to ensure that every Nigerian child is registered at birth and given a legal identity from the earliest stage of life. The stakeholders are pushing for stronger integration of birth registration with primary healthcare services, greater decentralisation of registration centres to local communities and seamless interoperability between civil registration and national identity systems. The renewed push is aimed particularly at newborns and children under one, with stakeholders stressing that timely birth registration can serve as the gateway to a child’s access to healthcare, education, social protection and other essential services. The initiative forms part of efforts to strengthen Nigeria’s civil registration and vital statistics system and close the gap that has left millions of children without proof of legal identity. At a media dialogue on birth registration for children under one year, UNICEF Child Protection Specialist, Mr. Denis Onoise, said the challenge was not simply about parents failing to register their children, but also about removing barriers that make registration difficult for families. Onoise identified inadequate registration centres, long distances to service points, language barriers, inefficient registration processes and insufficient financial, human and material resources among factors limiting access to civil registration services. He said: “The main challenges to accelerate civil registration and legal identity in Nigeria include limited accessibility to civil registration services, inadequate number of registration centres and associated long distances, language barriers, inefficient registration processes, and insufficient financial, human capacity and material resources.” According to him, families also bear indirect costs, including transportation, time away from work and repeated journeys to registration points. “The problem is compounded in hard-to-reach areas and among disadvantaged population groups,” he added. The stakeholders, however, are seeking to turn the challenge into an opportunity by connecting birth registration with the country’s broader identity management system. Under the proposed stronger collaboration, NPC would oversee birth and death registration, while NIMC would facilitate the linkage of registered births to the national identity database and prompt assignment of the National Identification Number (NIN). Local governments would play a critical role by bringing registration services closer to families through ward and community-level registration points and integrating birth registration into primary healthcare services. The approach is expected to reduce the burden on parents and ensure that registration becomes part of routine services provided when a child is born or taken to a health facility. The partnership also involved UNICEF, which provides technical, financial and technological support, while Barnksforte Technologies Limited supports the development and deployment of the electronic civil registration and vital statistics system. The stakeholders particularly advocated the integration of birth registration into primary healthcare, where mothers and newborns already interact with the health system. Under the proposed model, birth notification at a health facility or community level would trigger the registration process, followed by issuance of a birth certificate and linkage with the national identity system. This, they said, would make birth registration less dependent on parents making separate journeys to registration centres. The strategy is also expected to improve the accuracy and timeliness of population data required for planning healthcare, education, social protection and other government programmes. The stakeholders said birth registration goes beyond obtaining a certificate. According to Onoise birth record establishes a child’s identity, including name, sex, place and date of birth, and provides the foundation for recognition before the law. He said without legal identity, children may face difficulties proving their age or identity and can become more vulnerable to exclusion from education, healthcare, social protection and justice systems. In his presentation, he further noted that an estimated 24.8 million Nigerian children under five have been registered. Such children, it warned, may also face increased vulnerability to child marriage, trafficking, child labour, abuse, exploitation and family separation. He said stakeholders are also relying on digitalisation to expand coverage and improve efficiency. He explained that: “An interoperable digital civil registration system would enable registration records to be securely shared across relevant government systems while maintaining data protection and confidentiality. “The approach is expected to reduce duplication, improve data quality and make it easier to track births from notification through registration, certificate issuance and identity enrolment.” He however, acknowledged that gaps remain. He noted that health-facility interoperability had stalled in some areas, with none of 371 targeted facilities live at the time of the assessment, while the birth notification pipeline was yet to record notifications in the reporting year. There was also a significant gap between registrations and certificates issued, with 443,162 registrations compared with 120,469 certificates issued. He further noted that parents remain key in the reforms being proposed. He stressed that government systems alone cannot achieve universal birth registration. Parents and caregivers remain central to ensuring that every birth is registered promptly. He urged parents to take advantage of registration services when available at health facilities, local government offices and community registration points, while calling on traditional and religious leaders, women’s groups, young people and the media to strengthen public awareness. He also called for stronger domestic financing, recruitment of permanent registrars, improved coordination among agencies and sustained community mobilisation. He explained that the overall objective was to make birth registration a simple, accessible and routine part of every child’s entry into life, ensuring that no child grows up without a recognised identity. The post Birth registration: NPC, UNICEF unite to give every child legal identity appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kofi Tonto explains $800 embassy payment, denies link to alleged $19m fraud
items.description: Former Head of Information and Public Affairs at Ghana’s Embassy in Washington and New Patriotic Party (NPP) communicator, Kofi Tonto, has denied any involvement in an alleged fraudulent scheme said to have resulted in the loss of approximately US$19 million at the embassy. Mr Tonto’s denial follows reports alleging that he received US$800 from funds linked to the purported scheme uncovered through a forensic audit conducted by the Ghana Audit Service into the affairs of the embassy between 2017 and 2025. In a statement issued in Accra on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, Mr Tonto said he had never been involved in any scheme involving the sharing or receipt of illicit funds. “I have never been involved in any scheme, the sharing of, or the receipt of any ill-obtained funds,” he said. Mr Tonto also noted that he was not named as a person of interest for investigation in the audit report. According to him, the US$800 he received in July 2021 was a legitimate child benefit payment following the birth of his daughter in January 2021. He explained that the payment was part of an established practice at the embassy, noting that about 28 other staff members had also received similar benefits for various life-changing events. He said he neither solicited the payment nor determined the amount, the receiving bank account or the source of the funds. Mr Tonto therefore argued that the one-time US$800 payment could not be used as a basis to implicate him in an alleged fraudulent scheme involving US$19 million. He further clarified that all payments he received during his tenure at the embassy—including compensation, allowances, benefits and refunds—were made in accordance with established procedures. He said the payments he received between March 2019 and July 2021 were made in good faith and that he was never involved in decisions concerning the financial management of the embassy, particularly the operation or closure of any bank account. Mr Tonto has consequently urged his family, friends, admirers and the general public to disregard what he described as a distorted narrative seeking to falsely attribute wrongdoing to him. He maintained that the allegations do not accurately reflect his role or involvement in the affairs of Ghana’s Embassy in Washington.

items.title: Osun election: Adeleke’s campaign spokesman threatens N10bn suit against Fadahunsi
items.description: Pelumi Olajengbesi, a campaign spokesman for Governor Ademola Adeleke’s re-election, has threatened a ₦10bn suit against the lawmaker representing Osun East Senatorial District, Francis Fadahunsi, “for defamation and injurious falsehood”. In a letter dated August 12, 2026 and addressed to the lawmaker by Olajengbesi’s lawyer, Hammed Lasisi, Esq., Olajengbesi considered certain statements made by Fadahunsi about him during live television interviews on Viable TV on 2nd July 2026 and Channels Television’s Politics Today on 11th August 2026 as malicious and injurious to his personality. Olajengbesi demanded an immediate retraction of the statements and an unequivocal public apology within 24 hours, after which legal proceedings would be instituted. The letter read, “On 2nd July 2026, our Client’s attention was drawn to a live interview granted by you and aired on Viable TV, which was subsequently reproduced, republished and widely disseminated through Facebook, TikTok, WhatsApp, X, Instagram and other social and digital media platforms. “During the said interview, you launched a direct attack on the identity, character and reputation of our Client by stating, among other things, that our Client was “not even from the same Ijebu-Jesha” and was “from somewhere in Ogun State.” You further accused him of “using thugs, Eiye and Aye.” “These statements directly questioned our Client’s identity and origin as a son of Ijebu-Jesa and, more gravely, imputed that he sponsors, associates with and/or deploys thugs and members of the Eiye and Aye cult groups in furtherance of his political activities. “Again, on 11th August 2026, during your live appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today, you made another direct statement concerning our Client while commenting on the late Ajayi Aderogba, also known as Rogba, to wit: ‘Rogba is an Eiye man sponsored by Barr. Olajengbesi terrorising the whole … my own territory up and down through all these Eiye and Aye.’ “The natural, ordinary and unmistakable meaning conveyed by the above statement is that our Client sponsors, finances, supports and/or patronises members of the Eiye and Aye cult groups and deploys them to terrorise members of the public.” Olajengbesi denied these allegations as false, defamatory and gravely injurious to his personal, professional and political reputation. “The allegation of sponsoring cultists and persons engaged in acts of terror is particularly serious, as it imputes criminality and conduct wholly incompatible with our Client’s standing as a legal practitioner, public figure and candidate for elective office. Olajengbesi said he has never sponsored, financed, supported, patronised or otherwise provided resources to any cult group or its members for criminal, political or other unlawful activities. Neither has he authorised any person to terrorise, intimidate or attack members of the public on his behalf. Olajengbesi demanded that Fadahunsi retract the defamatory statements through the same media and platforms by which they were published and/or disseminated, and publish an unequivocal and unreserved public apology through appropriate national media and social media platforms. Olajengbesi’s lawyer said that if he fails to do so within 24 hours, he will approach the court to compel Fadahunsi to pay ₦10,000,000,000.00 (Ten Billion Naira) as general and aggravated damages for defamation and injurious falsehood. items.title: Maurice: face aux difficultés économiques, de plus en plus de jeunes cherchent à émigrer
items.description: L’envie de partir gagne du terrain chez les jeunes Mauriciens. Selon le dernier rapport de l’Afrobarometer, rendu public lundi 10 août à Réduit, Maurice, 76 % des 18-25 ans ont pensé, à des degrés divers, à émigrer. Cela fait trois fois plus qu’il y a 10 ans. Emploi, études, difficultés économiques ou encore coût de la vie figurent parmi les principales motivations. Un chiffre qui contraste avec l’image d’une île stable et prospère, souvent présentée comme un modèle dans la région. Certains observateurs voient une crise de confiance plus profonde dans l’économie, les institutions, mais aussi dans la capacité du pays à offrir des perspectives à sa jeunesse.

items.title: Propos d’une maire sénégalaise à l’encontre des étalagistes guinéens : le virus de la xénophobie sud-africaine aurait-elle atteint le pays de la Téranga ?
items.description: Dans une vidéo devenue virale sur les réseaux sociaux, une maire sénégalaise, lors d'une opération de déguerpissement, s'en prend aux commerçants qui s'installent dans des endroits inappropriés. Si, sur le plan purement légal, elle pourrait avoir raison, les propos qui accompagnent cependant son acte inquiètent plus d'un, car ils visent particulièrement la communauté guinéenne. Surtout que ces propos interviennent au moment où des appels à la haine et des menaces d'expulsion visant cette même communauté gagnent du terrain dans ce pays voisin et circulent sur les réseaux sociaux. Des plateformes xénophobes et répugnantes, suivies par des milliers de personnes, ont été créées à cet effet sur TikTok, WhatsApp et autres. Certains Africains oublient l'histoire si particulière et si délicate du continent, et il faut faire très attention. Il ne faut pas tomber dans le piège tendu par la colonisation, qui a créé des frontières artificielles séparant aujourd’hui des peuples africains qui sont pourtant les mêmes. D'ailleurs, quelle est la différence entre le Peul du Mali, de la Guinée, du Burkina Faso, du Niger et autres, et celui du Sénégal ? Quelle est la différence entre le Malinké de la Guinée, du Sénégal, de la Côte d'Ivoire, de la Gambie, du Burkina Faso, du Libéria, de la Sierra Leone, etc., si ce n'est celle différence inventée, provoquée par les Blancs pour nous affaiblir ? Les Africains doivent faire très attention. Alors que l'idéal devrait être de suivre la voie tracée par les pères fondateurs du continent, ce n’est pas maintenant qu'il faut se disperser autour d'idées ou de comportements qui ne nous avancent en rien. À dire vrai, cette situation préoccupante qui se développe actuellement au Sénégal doit interpeller plus d'un. En effet, le silence des autorités sénégalaises face à ce phénomène intrigue plus d'un. Si le silence du président sud-africain face à la montée de la xénophobie en Afrique du Sud est à condamner avec la dernière énergie, il en va de même pour le silence du président sénégalais face à la montée des discours de haine, de division et de stigmatisation visant notamment les Guinéens. En résumé, si les Africains ne prennent la mesure de la chose, s'ils ne prennent pas leurs responsabilités pour préserver les liens et les relations fraternelles qui les unissent depuis la nuit des temps, ils ne sont plus loin de l'implosion. Évidemment, si chaque Africain rejette un autre peuple africain pour des raisons subjectives, à quoi servent alors l'Union africaine, la CEDEAO et toutes ces organisations africaines ? Sayon MARA, Juriste L’article Propos d'une maire sénégalaise à l'encontre des étalagistes guinéens : le virus de la xénophobie sud-africaine aurait-elle atteint le pays de la Téranga ? est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Akosua Manu questions abandonment of Zipline and Agenda 111 amid rising maternal deaths
items.description: Former Vice President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia’s Advisor on Gender and Social Protection, Akosua Manu, has questioned the reported disruption of the Zipline medical drone programme and the slow progress of Agenda 111, amid rising maternal deaths in Ghana. Her comments follow a Ghana Health Service report that 965 women died from pregnancy-related complications in 2025. Ms Manu says the figure should prompt the government to reconsider interventions that could improve access to emergency healthcare. “965. That’s how many Ghanaian women died from pregnancy-related complications in 2025 alone. Mothers. Daughters. Wives. Sisters. Women who walked into our health system carrying life and never walked back out,” She said in a Facebook post. Ms Manu said the drone programme, championed by Dr Bawumia, was designed to ensure critical supplies such as blood and emergency medicines reach health facilities quickly. “By championing Zipline, he placed the value of human lives ahead of the narrow calculation of cost, recognising that when a mother is haemorrhaging, the most expensive intervention is the one that arrives too late.” She also said the abandoned Agenda 111 hospitals are intended to bring healthcare facilities closer to underserved communities. “Ghana needs a health system that is both physically accessible and technologically enabled. We need functioning hospitals in underserved communities, but we also need the technology and logistics to ensure those hospitals have the blood, medicines and other supplies required when emergencies arise.” she noted. She added that: “If there are real problems with the cost or management of Zipline, fix them. If there are problems with Agenda 111, resolve them and complete the hospitals. If there is something better, show us and deploy it.” Ms Manu believes that the rising maternal deaths should serve as a wake-up call for Ghana to prioritise solutions that can improve access to emergency healthcare rather than the politics surrounding it.

items.title: Migration : le Maroc met en garde contre les appels du 15 août et appelle l’Espagne à rapatrier les mineurs
items.description: Le ministère de l’Intérieur a affirmé, mercredi, avoir renforcé le dispositif de sécurité vers les villes de Sebta et Melilla et a prévenu que les participants et les personnes qui organisent ou promeuvent les appels des tentatives de franchissement collectif et illégal pourront faire l’objet de poursuites. Il a également appelé l'Espagne à « assumer ses responsabilités » et à accélérer les procédures permettant le retour des mineurs marocains. Dans une déclaration, le porte-parole du ministère de l’Intérieur dont Hespress FR détient une copie, est revenu sur les appels répétés sur les réseaux sociaux pour organiser des tentatives de migration collective le 15 août 2026. Le ministère affirme suivre ces événements de près , tout en prévenant que « toutes les mesures nécessaires ont été prises afin de faire face à toute tentative de franchissement illégal et d’intercepter toute personne cherchant à y participer ». Dans sa déclaration, le ministère de l’Intérieur a indiqué avoir constaté au cours des derniers jours, la circulation de publications et de messages anonymes sur certains réseaux sociaux, soulignant que ces « initiatives présentent de sérieux risques pour la sécurité des personnes et cherchent à exploiter les questions migratoires à des fins d’incitation, passibles de sanctions prévues par la loi ». « Les mesures juridiques nécessaires seront également prises à l’encontre de toute personne reconnue coupable d’actes contraires à la loi, y compris les auteurs et promoteurs de tels appels sur les réseaux sociaux », a indiqué le porte-parole. « Le ministère appelle chacun à faire preuve de vigilance et de responsabilité et à ne pas se laisser entraîner par ce type d’appels suspects et trompeurs, qui pourraient mettre des vies humaines en danger », ajoute la même source en affirmant que la lutte contre l’immigration irrégulière est menée dans le respect de la loi et dans le souci de protéger la sécurité des personnes. Des arrestations et un dispositif sécuritaire renforcé Il annonce par ailleurs que les autorités ont déjà procédé à l’arrestation de plusieurs personnes soupçonnées d’avoir mené des actions d’incitation. Ces personnes ont été soumises à une procédure d’enquête judiciaire sous la supervision du parquet compétent, souligne la même source. Le ministère affirme avoir mis en place un dispositif de vigilance permanente et pas seulement pour la période du 15 août, notamment dans les zones proches des points de passage de Sebta et Melilla. Et d'insister que ce passage est « constamment renforcé et adapté en fonction de l’évolution de la situation et de la nature des risques constatés ». Le document précise que la lutte contre l’immigration irrégulière et les réseaux de traite des êtres humains « ne peut reposer sur les efforts d’une seule partie » et qu'elle exige que toutes les parties assument leurs responsabilités et respectent leurs engagements, dans le cadre d’un partage des responsabilités. Un appel lancé à l'Espagne « Le ministère de l’Intérieur appelle les autorités espagnoles, dans le cadre de la coordination et de la coopération existant entre les deux pays, à assumer leurs responsabilités et à accélérer les procédures permettant le retour auprès de leurs familles au Maroc des mineurs non accompagnés présents à Sebta, dans le respect de leur intérêt supérieur », a exhorté le porte parole. Rabat appelle également à surmonter les obstacles administratifs et judiciaires qui empêchent leur retour dans les meilleurs délais. Se disant conscient que la lutte contre les défis liés à l’immigration irrégulière constitue une responsabilité partagée nécessitant une coopération effective et équilibrée ainsi qu’un engagement mutuel de toutes les parties, et compte tenu des résultats et effets positifs du mécanisme de retour immédiat, le ministère réaffirme l’importance centrale de ce dispositif, dont l’efficacité et la contribution concrète à la gestion des défis rencontrés et au renforcement des interventions sur le terrain ont été démontrées par les expériences précédentes. Enfin, le ministère de l’Intérieur affirme que les autorités marocaines continueront à assumer leurs responsabilités avec fermeté et sens des responsabilités, afin de garantir la protection de l’ordre public, des personnes et des biens, de lutter contre l’immigration irrégulière et les réseaux de traite des êtres humains, tout en maintenant le plus haut niveau de vigilance, de préparation et de coordination permanente face aux différents risques, dans le strict respect des dispositions de la loi.
