items.title: Fact Check: CJ’s warrant doesn’t limit vacation judge, Justice Achibonga, to specific cases
items.description: A warrant issued by Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie authorising a judge to sit during the 2026 legal vacation does not restrict the judge to emergency applications or interlocutory matters. The document, dated 23rd July, 2026, and addressed to Justice Francis Apongabuno Achibonga and cited by JoyNews , authorises him to sit as an additional High Court judge at the Specialised Court ‘1’ at the Law Court Complex in Accra during the legal vacation. Justice Achibonga is the vacation judge currently presiding over the trial of former National Signals Bureau Director Kwabena Adu-Boahene and his wife, the very case that lead counsel Samuel Atta Akyea has boycotted, sparking the ongoing dispute over vacation court proceedings. It states: “By virtue of the powers conferred upon me, I hereby authorise you to sit as an additional High Court Judge at the Specialised Court ‘1’, Law Court Complex, Accra, during the 2026 Legal Vacation and conduct hearings.” The warrant does not identify particular cases the judge is required to hear, nor does it expressly limit proceedings to emergencies, motions or interlocutory applications. The wording is significant amid claims by private legal practitioner Samuel Atta Akyea that substantive and part-heard cases should ordinarily not continue during the legal vacation. Speaking on JoyNews’ Top Story , Mr Atta Akyea argued that vacation judges traditionally dealt with urgent matters rather than substantive trials. “All the part-heard cases in the realm, they’ve gone to bed. I’m telling you, part-heard cases, the judges are not hearing part-heard cases in the vacation. It’s as clear as daylight,” he said. He also questioned why some cases were proceeding during the vacation and described the situation as “selective justice”. “Why do we have to change this thing because there are some special cases in the eyes of somebody and there are some special judges who should continue working? What is the emergency about this case? … I’ll not be part of it,” he said. The contents of the warrant, however, show that Justice Achibonga’s authority is broadly stated as the power to “conduct hearings” at the designated court during the legal vacation. While the document does not, by itself, settle the broader debate over the traditional scope of Vacation Court proceedings, it does not contain the restrictions suggested in arguments that vacation judges are authorised only to hear emergency or interlocutory matters. The issue forms part of an ongoing disagreement between the Ghana Bar Association (GBA) and the judiciary over court sittings during the legal vacation. The GBA has maintained that Vacation Courts traditionally deal with emergencies and interlocutory matters rather than substantive trials, and has also argued that the availability of counsel should be taken into account. Deputy Attorney-General Dr Justice Srem-Sai has challenged that position, maintaining that the authority to determine whether court proceedings should take place rests with the bench rather than lawyers. The Chief Justice has similarly defended the authority of judges who have been duly authorised to sit during the vacation. Justice Achibonga’s warrant confirms that he has been authorised to sit as an additional High Court judge at the Specialised Court ‘1’ and “conduct hearings” during the 2026 legal vacation.

items.title: ‘No pressure at all’ – Björkegren as Ghana’s Black Queens chase World Cup lifeline
items.description: Ghana coach Kim Lars Björkegren says he is feeling “no pressure at all” ahead of the Black Queens’ crucial 2027 Women’s World Cup play-off against Ivory Coast on Thursday. The Women’s senior national team will face their West African rivals in Casablanca, Morocco, with a place in the intercontinental World Cup play-offs at stake. The match offers the Queens another route to the 2027 global tournament in Brazil after their hopes of securing automatic qualification were ended by Malawi in the quarter-finals of the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations. “For me personally, to be honest, no pressure at all,” Björkegren said during the pre-match conference. “I do not feel pressure because if I feel pressure, I can’t make the right decisions. “I have been in this game for 20 years as a coach and 10 years as a player, that is my whole life.” The winner against Ivory Coast will advance to the intercontinental play-offs, where they will face teams from other continents for a place at the tournament. Ghana has not qualified for the competition since 2007.

items.title: Iranian photojournalist faces 15 years in prison over images, reporting
items.description: By Nilo Tabrizy LONDON, Aug 12 (Reuters) - Acclaimed Iranian photojournalist Yalda Moaiery has spent much of her career documenting moments of dissent and the lives of women in Iran. The work has repeatedly brought her into conflict with the authorities, and on Iran's National Journalist Day on Saturday she learned she had been sentenced to 15 years in prison. The sentence was handed down under a law enacted after a 12-day war between Israel and Iran in 2025, legislation that Iranian authorities say is intended to combat espionage and cooperation with hostile states.

items.title: Counsellor Perfect, Rev Annan speak on what keeps love alive in marriage
items.description: Counsellor Perfect and Rev. Daniel Annan have urged couples to reflect on responsibility, sacrifice and sincerity in marriage during a discussion on Let’s Talk on Joy Prime. The conversation, which explored whether love can fade or diminish in marriage, began with a case of a husband who feels his wife no longer loves him, but evolved into a wider reflection on what sustains relationships. Counsellor Perfect challenged couples to pay closer attention to what they learn about each other before saying “I do”. She stressed that people must not only fall in love but also take time to understand the person they intend to marry. According to her, “If you fear God, it is difficult to react” in certain hurtful ways, because the fear of God should influence how a person responds to their partner, particularly during difficult moments. She also made a striking observation about women and relationships, saying, “Women are moved by what they can get, not what they can give.” Her point, however, went beyond material things. Counsellor Perfect explained that when a woman is genuinely in love, her actions begin to reveal it. “A woman is in love when you begin to see that she does everything genuinely without complaining,” she said, pointing to sincerity and sacrifice as some of the clearest signs of genuine love. For her, love is often revealed in quiet, consistent actions. She said when a woman truly loves her partner, sincerity and a willingness to make sacrifices become evident, not necessarily through grand gestures but through everyday care, support and contribution without keeping score. Rev. Daniel Annan, however, brought another dimension to the discussion. He encouraged couples to examine their own contributions to the marriage instead of immediately concluding that their partner had stopped loving them. His counsel centred on responsibility and reflection, reminding couples that what appears to be a disappearance of love may be linked to changes in behaviour, attention and effort within the marriage. He urged couples to revisit the things they did when the relationship was still thriving and ask whether those efforts have disappeared. According to Rev. Annan, returning to those responsibilities and intentional actions could help couples rediscover what they have gradually lost. The discussion became more emotional when callers shared personal experiences of love, disappointment and sacrifice, describing moments when they felt they were giving more than they were receiving. At one point, host Asieduwaa Akumia became visibly emotional and teary as she listened to the stories, reflecting the depth of feeling expressed by callers. The atmosphere in the studio shifted from routine discussion to a deeply personal exchange. Ultimately, the conversation underscored a central message: love must be demonstrated, not only declared. Counsellor Perfect emphasised sincerity and sacrifice, while Rev. Annan called for self-examination and a return to the habits that once strengthened relationships. Together, their counsel suggested that before concluding that love has disappeared, couples should ask a difficult question: what have I stopped doing that I used to do when I was deeply in love? Sometimes, the way back to love begins with returning to the beginning.

items.title: INEC reprints Osun ballot papers, result sheets to accommodate SDP candidate
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC said it has commenced the reproduction of ballot papers for the Osun State Governorship Election to accommodate the candidate of the Social Democratic Party SDP, Dr Francis Olugbenga Ajala, and his running mate, Faseke Babajimi Oladipo, who have now been added to the ballot. In a statement signed by the National Commissioner and Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee at INEC, Mohammed Kudu Haruna, the Commission said the action was taken in compliance with the judgment of the Federal High Court, Abuja, delivered on 22nd July 2026 in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/344/2026, in a matter between the Social Democratic Party and Dr Francis Olugbenga Ajala on one hand, and INEC on the other. According to the statement, the court had ordered the Commission to forthwith recognise, accept, upload, process and publish the name and particulars of Dr Ajala as the candidate of the SDP for the election. “The Commission wishes to inform the public that the reproduced ballot papers will arrive in Osun State on Thursday, 13th August 2026, and will, same day, be moved to Local Government Area offices across the State, in line with its standard distribution procedure ahead of the election,” the statement read. With the addition of the SDP candidate, the total number of political parties contesting the governorship election, scheduled for Saturday, 15th August 2026, now stands at 15. INEC noted that the result sheets for the election are also being reproduced alongside the ballot papers to reflect the inclusion of the SDP candidate. The Commission assured political parties, candidates and the general public of its commitment to conducting a free, fair and credible election in Osun State. items.title: Ondo Govt warns monarchs against running detention centres, courts
items.description: — Stop land grabbing, self-help in palaces — Provide intelligence, not act as security agencies By Dayo Johnson, Akure AKURE — The Ondo State Government has warned traditional rulers in the state against turning their palaces into detention centres or operating parallel courts. The Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice, Dr Kayode Ajulo, SAN, gave the warning at a three-day workshop for traditional rulers in Akure, with the theme, “Repositioning the Traditional Institution for Harmonious Communal Relationship, Security, Cultural Preservation and Sustainable Development.” Ajulo said no traditional ruler had the power to order the indefinite detention of anyone accused of stealing, insulting the palace, owing money, violating community rules or being involved in a dispute. He urged traditional rulers to focus on peacebuilding, intelligence gathering and cooperation with law enforcement agencies rather than investigating, detaining or punishing suspects. “An Oba does not lose dignity by listening to both sides of a dispute. Fair hearing must be observed in traditional administration,” he said. The Attorney General advised the monarchs to embrace mediation and customary arbitration, but stressed that such processes must be voluntary and should not replace judicial adjudication. On land matters, Ajulo cautioned against using customary authority to justify self-help, forceful entry, intimidation or illegal occupation. He urged traditional rulers to refer land-related cases to the appropriate statutory bodies, including the Anti-Land Grabbing Task Force. The commissioner reminded the monarchs that the Constitution does not recognise traditional rulers as a “fourth arm of government.” He said their roles included serving as custodians of culture, peacebuilders, mediators and community mobilisers. “Traditional rulers should see themselves as custodians of history and culture, not as alternative courts or government institutions,” Ajulo stated. On security, he urged the monarchs to provide credible intelligence to the government and security agencies on issues including kidnapping, cultism, communal clashes, illegal mining and farmer-herder conflicts. He, however, warned them against acting as alternative security agencies. Ajulo said traditional institutions could also contribute to development by attracting investment, resolving disputes, protecting investors, promoting agriculture, safeguarding natural resources and supporting youth entrepreneurship. He stressed that repositioning the traditional institution was not intended to diminish the authority of the palace, but to ensure that its moral and cultural influence was exercised within the law. items.title: Government weaponising judiciary against NPP – Awal Mohammed
items.description: A member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) Communications Team, Awal Mohammed, has accused the government of weaponising the judiciary against the party, describing the continued prosecution of cases involving former NPP appointees as “selective justice”. Speaking on JoyNews’ AM Show on Wednesday, August 12, Mr Mohammed questioned the basis for allowing some criminal cases involving former NPP officials to continue during the legal vacation. He argued that authorities had not demonstrated that similar cases had previously been treated in the same manner. According to him, the concern was not whether the cases were criminal, but why particular cases appeared to be receiving special attention. “The question is: why the selective agency?” he asked. Mr Mohammed also argued that other serious criminal cases, including murder and rape, were before the courts and questioned why cases involving former NPP officials should be prioritised. “Why are these cases so special? Not even murder. Not even rape,” he said. He further raised concerns about the possible implications of prolonged legal proceedings, including issues relating to national security. Mr Mohammed said the cases involving former NPP appointees were already being handled as specialised matters, with the accused persons appearing in court regularly. “Now the state, together with the Chief Justice, is saying that these specialised cases against former NPP appointees must continue,” he said. He maintained that the approach reinforced his view that the government was using the judicial process selectively against members of the NPP.

items.title: GRA outlines who qualifies for Modified Taxation Scheme and how it works
items.description: The Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) has outlined the categories of taxpayers who qualify for the Modified Taxation Scheme, as well as those who are excluded from the system. Chief Revenue Officer of the GRA’s Domestic Tax Revenue Division, Victor Yao Akogo, explained the scheme on the Joy FM Super Morning Show on Wednesday, August 12, as part of a discussion on the Modified Taxation Scheme. According to Mr Akogo, the scheme is mainly designed for resident individuals who earn business income, particularly those operating in the informal sector. “When you talk about the Modified Taxation Scheme, we are emphasising business income of resident individuals,” he said. Mr Akogo said a person must meet a number of conditions to qualify. First, the person must be a resident of Ghana and must earn business income from Ghana. The individual must also not be registered for Value Added Tax (VAT). “So to qualify to be part of the Modified Taxation, you must be a resident of Ghana and must also earn business income. You must not be registered for VAT,” he explained. He added that the scheme is particularly relevant to people operating in the informal sector who are not required to register for VAT. “It means that your turnover should not be more than GH₵750,000 per annum,” Mr Akogo said. This means that resident individuals earning business income, operating mainly in the informal sector and with annual turnover of no more than GH¢750,000, may fall under the Modified Taxation Scheme, provided they meet the other requirements. Mr Akogo also outlined categories of people who are not eligible to operate under the scheme. Professionals, including engineers, accountants and lawyers, are excluded because they are regulated and are expected to be able to keep proper records of their businesses. “If you are a professional, an engineer, accountant, lawyer, you are not part of the Modified Taxation Scheme because you are regulated and you can keep records,” he said. People who choose to leave the scheme are also allowed to do so under the law. “If you decide to opt out from the Modified Taxation Scheme, the law allows you to opt out,” Mr Akogo explained. He further said people with multiple businesses do not qualify for the scheme. Those operating more than one outlet are also excluded. “If you have multiple businesses, you are not supposed to be part of the Modified Taxation Scheme. And in addition to that, if you have more than one outlet, then you should not be part of the Modified Taxation Scheme,” he said. In summary, the excluded groups include professionals such as lawyers and accountants, people with multiple businesses, those operating from more than one outlet, and individuals who have opted out of the scheme. Mr Akogo said the Modified Taxation Scheme is divided into three main categories. “We have three categories under the Modified Taxation Scheme. We have the presumptive tax based on installments. We have the presumptive by turnover. And we also have the modified cash basis,” he said. The first category covers resident individuals whose annual business income is up to GH¢20,000. Under this arrangement, taxpayers pay a fixed amount rather than having their tax calculated directly from their business expenses or profits. “The presumptive by installment is for those taxpayers or resident individuals whose business income is up to 20,000 Ghana cedis per annum, and they pay a fixed amount as tax for the year,” Mr Akogo said. “The fixed amount they pay is 45 Ghana cedis a quarter,” he added. This category includes small traders such as people selling from tabletops and those operating small shops. “Those selling on tabletop and those selling in small shops. So they are those that pay by installment. So we call them presumptive tax by installment,” he explained. The second category is for taxpayers whose annual turnover is above GH¢20,000 but does not exceed GH¢750,000. Mr Akogo said people in this category pay three per cent of their annual turnover as tax. “The second category is the presumptive tax by turnover. This category of taxpayers are persons whose turnover are more than GH¢20,000, but not exceeding GH¢750,000 for the year. They pay three percent of their turnover as tax for the whole year,” he said. He explained that the system is intended for taxpayers who may not be able to maintain detailed business records. “Because they cannot keep records, because they are not regulated, we say every sales, every turnover they earn, three percent of it must be the tax they pay for the whole year,” Mr Akogo said. The third category is the modified cash basis. This applies to taxpayers who have some knowledge of record-keeping and want their business expenses to be taken into account when determining their taxable income. “This category claim they have knowledge about how to keep limited records, and therefore they want to be considered for their expenses that they incur,” Mr Akogo said. Under this system, the normal principles for assessing tax are applied. The taxpayer’s allowable business expenses are deducted to determine the chargeable income, after which the appropriate graduated tax rate is applied. “So standard rules of assessment of tax is applied on them. So we say that they determine, we determine their assessable income, we allow them expenses that they incur in running their business, and arrive at their chargeable income, and then we apply a graduated rate to the chargeable income,” he explained. Mr Akogo said the graduated tax rate ranges from five per cent to 35 per cent. “The graduated rate, the highest rate is 35 percent, and the smallest rate is five percent,” he said. He added that the modified cash basis gives eligible taxpayers an opportunity to account for expenses incurred in running their businesses. “So the modified cash will give you the opportunity to have access to expenses you incurred in running the business, but you pay tax based on a graduated rate. The higher the income that you earn, the higher you pay as tax,” he said.

items.title: Tunisie | Le combat pour l’égalité en matière d’héritage se poursuit
items.description: Pour Raja Dahmani, présidente de l’Association tunisienne des femmes démocrates (ATFD), le combat pour l’adoption d’une loi instaurant l’égalité en matière d’héritage entre l’homme et la femme se poursuivra et son association continuera de soulever cette question. Intervenant ce mercredi 12 août 2026 lors d’un séminaire international organisé à Tunis sur le thème «Où en sommes-nous de l'égalité ?» , à l’occasion de la célébration du 70 e anniversaire du Code du statut personnel (CSP) — auquel ont pris part des femmes défenseures des droits humains, des avocates et des militantes venues de Tunisie ainsi que de divers pays arabes et de la région —, Mme Dahmani a ajouté que l’ATFD réclame depuis longtemps une révision du CSP. Ce texte pionnier dans le monde arabo-musulman, a permis de réaliser des avancées sociales en consacrant l’égalité sur certains plans, mais il présente, selon elle, des lacunes et contient des dispositions discriminatoires devant être abrogées. Le séminaire devrait d’ailleurs aboutir à l’élaboration de la «Déclaration de Tunis sur l’égalité au sein de la famille» . Rappelons dans ce contexte que, sous la présidence de Béji Caïd Essebsi, entre 2015 et 2019, un projet de loi pour l’instauration de l’égalité entre l’homme et la femme en matière d’héritage, a achoppé à un conservatisme religieux et social ambiant et n’a pu être adopté dans sa mouture initiale. I. B. 70 ans après | Le combat recommencé pour les droits des femmes en Tunisie L’article Tunisie | Le combat pour l’égalité en matière d’héritage se poursuit est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: FDA calls for stronger support for breastfeeding as Ghana marks World Breastfeeding Week
items.description: The Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) has called for stronger measures to protect, promote and support breastfeeding as Ghana joins the global community to commemorate World Breastfeeding Week 2026. According to a press statement issued on Wednesday, August 12, this year’s observance is being held under the theme, “Breastfeeding for a Sustainable Start in Life: Strengthen What Works”, which urges governments, healthcare professionals, employers, families, communities and development partners to reinforce policies and programmes that have proven effective in improving breastfeeding outcomes. The FDA said sustained investment in interventions with measurable impact was necessary to maintain progress and address emerging challenges affecting breastfeeding practices. According to the Authority, breastfeeding remains one of the most effective and cost-efficient public health interventions for improving child survival, nutrition and development. It noted that breast milk provides the nutrients infants need during the first six months of life and helps protect them against diarrhoeal diseases, respiratory infections, childhood obesity and other illnesses. The FDA also stressed the importance of continued breastfeeding alongside appropriate complementary feeding up to two years and beyond, saying the practice contributes to healthy growth, cognitive development and long-term well-being. The Authority said the benefits of breastfeeding extend beyond children, with mothers also gaining significant health benefits. Breastfeeding can reduce the risk of breast and ovarian cancers, support recovery after childbirth and strengthen the emotional bond between mothers and their children. The FDA further linked breastfeeding to environmental sustainability, describing breast milk as a natural and renewable source of infant nutrition that does not require manufacturing, packaging or transportation. It said promoting breastfeeding could therefore contribute to reducing environmental waste while supporting more sustainable food systems. Despite progress in Ghana’s breastfeeding practices following years of public health interventions, the FDA said several challenges continue to affect efforts to achieve optimal breastfeeding. These include aggressive marketing of breastmilk substitutes, changing lifestyles, workplace constraints, misinformation and inadequate support from families and communities. The Authority said it remained committed to protecting breastfeeding through the implementation and enforcement of the Breastfeeding Promotion Regulation, 2000 (L.I. 1667), which regulates the marketing and distribution of breastmilk substitutes in Ghana. The FDA said it would continue to monitor compliance, conduct market surveillance, educate stakeholders and work with partners to ensure mothers have access to accurate and evidence-based information on infant feeding. As part of the 2026 commemoration, the FDA said it would collaborate with the Ministry of Health, Ghana Health Service, Ubora Quality Institute, the media and other stakeholders on nationwide public education and regulatory enforcement. The campaign will also highlight innovations such as breastmilk banks, which have been established in some hospitals to make donated breast milk available to babies who need it. The FDA is urging health facilities to establish breastmilk banks as part of efforts to improve access to breast milk for infants. The Authority has called on mothers and caregivers to initiate breastfeeding within the first hour after birth, practise exclusive breastfeeding during the first six months and continue breastfeeding alongside appropriate complementary feeding up to two years or beyond, in line with national and international recommendations. Government institutions have also been urged to continue investing in policies and programmes that protect and support breastfeeding. Employers, meanwhile, have been encouraged to establish breastfeeding-friendly workplaces by providing flexible working arrangements, nursing breaks and safe, hygienic spaces where mothers can breastfeed or express and store breast milk. Healthcare professionals are expected to provide consistent, evidence-based counselling and support to mothers during pregnancy, childbirth and the postnatal period. The FDA also called on families and communities to provide the emotional, practical and social support mothers need to initiate and sustain breastfeeding. The media, it said, has a responsibility to provide accurate information, counter misinformation and promote positive messages about breastfeeding. Manufacturers, importers and distributors of breastmilk substitutes have been urged to comply with L.I. 1667 and adhere to ethical marketing practices that protect breastfeeding. The Authority also called for strong regulatory frameworks and enforcement of existing provisions governing breastmilk substitutes. The FDA said protecting breastfeeding was a shared responsibility requiring coordinated action across society. It maintained that supportive government policies, adequate healthcare support, breastfeeding-friendly workplaces, informed communities and strong family support could help create conditions in which mothers are better able to breastfeed successfully. The Authority said strengthening proven interventions would give children a better opportunity to survive, thrive and reach their full potential while contributing to healthier families and a more sustainable environment.

items.title: CBG commits GH¢55m to support 3,000 women, youth under GWYESCO programme
items.description: Consolidated Bank Ghana (CBG) has committed GH¢55 million to support about 3,000 women and young people under the Ghana Women and Youth Employment and Social Cohesion (GWYESCO) Programme. The initiative, which is being implemented by the Social Investment Fund (SIF), seeks to improve the resilience and living conditions of women and youth through job creation, entrepreneurship, access to finance and skills development. Speaking at the signing of a loan agreement in Accra on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, Managing Director of CBG, Dr Naomi Wolali Kwetey, said the bank would disburse the funds in phases over a 36-month period. She said the first tranche, representing about 25% of the total facility, would benefit approximately 800 beneficiaries. “Approximately GH¢55 million will be deployed over 36 months to support about 3,000 people. The first 25% advance will support about 800 beneficiaries. CBG is committed to a transparent selection process, sound credit appraisal, timely disbursement, and diligent monitoring,” she said. According to Dr Kwetey, the financing forms part of CBG’s commitment to supporting initiatives that promote economic inclusion and create opportunities for women and young people. “This partnership reflects our shared commitment to expanding access to funding for women, young people and micro, small and medium enterprises,” she said. The GWYESCO Programme, which will run from 2026 to 2028, targets young people aged between 18 and 35 and women aged 18 years and above. It will focus on training in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM), digital and creative skills, as well as improving access to finance for women- and youth-owned micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). The programme will be implemented in the Central and Eastern Regions, as well as Northern Ghana, covering the Upper West, Upper East and Savannah Regions. Beyond employment and entrepreneurship, GWYESCO is designed to promote peace-building and social cohesion, particularly in Northern Ghana, where communities face challenges associated with conflict, violent extremism, poverty and climate change. The programme also seeks to strengthen the capacity of institutions in monitoring and evaluation, environmental and social safeguards, and conflict prevention. Acting Chief Executive Officer of the Social Investment Fund, Abass Nurudeen, said the project was expected to receive funding from CBG, Apex Bank and Ghana Commercial Bank. He said CBG had taken the lead among the participating financial institutions by commencing the disbursement of funds for the programme. “Three financial institutions have been shortlisted to fund this (GWYESCO), the GCB, the CGB and the Apex Bank. Of all three, I am happy to say that it is CBG that has put us together to sign this,” he said. Mr Nurudeen said the financing would provide critical support to women and youth entrepreneurs while helping to address unemployment and other socio-economic vulnerabilities. The broader programme is expected to strengthen access to technical skills, business development services and finance, with the ultimate goal of creating sustainable livelihoods and improving social stability. The three-year intervention is therefore positioned as a strategic investment in Ghana’s women and youth, particularly those in regions facing higher levels of economic vulnerability and social risks.

items.title: PENGASSAN distributes cooking stoves, gas cylinders to disabled, indigent women in Abuja
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — OVER 200 people living with disabilities and indigent women in Kuje community of the Federal Capital Territory, FTC, Abuja, on Tuesday benefited from the Petroleum and Natural Gas Senior Staff Association of Nigeria, PENGASSAN Foundation. National Treasurer and Chairman of PENGASSAN Foundation*, Dr. David Owan, said they were in Kuje to show solidarity and bring gas and stoves to the indigent people to address health challenges caused by firewood Dr. Owan flanked by the National Chairperson, PENGASSAN Women Commission* and Secretary of the Foundation, Engr. Maryann Ada Mbanaso and the National Secretary of PENGASSAN Women Commission,* Comrade Chidinma Anyanwu distributed six kg cooking stoves/gas to the indigent women. Speaking at the palace of the 16th Gomo of Kuje, His Royal Highness, Dr. Haruna Tanko Jubrin, the Foundation chairman, said the solidarity and support to the beneficiaries was to combat respiratory health issues caused by the use of firewood. According to him, the use of firewood for cooking leads to respiratory problems and chronic conditions for women who inhale the smoke. He explained that the initiave was aimed at empowering women through cooking methods, reducing environmental impact and deforestation. He said that the Foundation funded solely by individual contributions of members seeks to help those who cannot afford the items. Owan emphasized the importance of using clean stoves to avoid the negative impacts of charcoal and firewood on health and the environment. He highlighted the impact of community development on the collection of firewood and how women are forced to travel further distances up to five to ten kilometers to collect firewood. He said the Foundation started in 2025 under the visionary leadership of the President of PENGASSAN, Comr. Engr. Festus Osifo, conducting various campaigns and activities, including hospital contributions and corporate social responsibility initiatives. “We decided we should give back to community. We need to do social corporate responsibility. Let our people know that we care about them. We are not government. It’s not our place to provide this. But we feel that if we are earning, we should reach out to other people. Let them get what we are getting equally,” he said. The Secretary of the Foundation, Engr. Mbanaso emphasized the role of women in cooking and the negative health impacts of using firewood such as premature aging and illnesses. She said the Foundation aims to empower women by providing better cooking methods to improve their health and living conditions. “Here, of course, you know that if you look around, you will see that the people we have on ground are women, and today we are talking about clean cooking. Actually, it is women that do more of the cooking because it’s our responsibility to provide and to cook for the family. “And when you look at what firewood does to women and does to our health, you find out that women get sick, a lot of l sicknesses arise from use of firewood in cooking. “So today we have come to empower them. We have come to say no to cooking with firewood and to give them a better way of cooking so that they will equally live and have better life for their children.” She further highlighted the security risks associated with women traveling long distances to collect firewood She expressed gratitude on behalf of the President of PENGASSAN, Comrade Engr. Festus Osifo for the orderly and respectful reception by the traditional ruler and his subjects. Also speaking, Secretary of *the PENGASSAN Women Commission, Comrade Chidinma Anyanwu encouraged beneficiaries to continue using the provided facilities to reduce deforestation and promote clean energy. She reiterated the fact that the Foundation is funded through PENGASSAN members salaries despite the tough economic times, adding that it was a way of showing their commitment to social responsibility. She attributed it to the visionary leadership of the PENGASSAN President, Comrade Osifo and the dedication of members of the association. Anyanwu said: “All these are happening under the visionary leadership of our President, Comrade Engineer Festus Osifo. So we say thank you to him for leading us in the right direction.” On his part, the Gomo of Kuje, Dr. Jubrin said the efforts of the Foundation contribute to to eradicate poverty in the community, stressing that it was a long-awaited opportunity for the community. He expressed the community’s appreciation to the PENGASSAN Foundation and continuous support. items.title: Police declare two men wanted over alleged Ikoyi murder
items.description: By Esther Onyegbula The Nigeria Police Force has declared two men, Ajibola Obateru and Folawiyo Balogun Alagbado, wanted over alleged conspiracy and murder in the Ikoyi axis of Lagos State. The declaration was contained in a Special Police Gazette Bulletin issued under the authority of the Inspector-General of Police and referenced Force Directive C.I.D. No. 48. The bulletin, with reference number CR: 3000/LSX/D18/VOL. 1/68, was issued through the Office of the Commissioner of Police, State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Musiliu Smith Street, Panti-Yaba, Lagos State. According to the police, the two suspects are wanted in connection with an incident in which a female victim was allegedly attacked and killed, with her body and personal belongings subsequently taken away. The police alleged that Ajibola Obateru, 33, conspired with others and attacked the victim before they allegedly made away with her body and personal belongings. The bulletin described Obateru as a Yoruba male, 5.9 feet tall, thinly built, with an oval face, long nose, small mouth, thin lips, black eyes, fair complexion and pointed chin. It further stated that he has thick black hair, a high head and high forehead, and “appears gentle” in his habits and mannerisms. His last known address was given as Ibadan, Oyo State. Similarly, the police declared Folawiyo Balogun Alagbado, 32, wanted over the same allegations. The police alleged that Balogun Alagbado conspired with others to attack the victim, who was allegedly killed, after which her body was taken to an unknown location. The bulletin also alleged that the victim’s belongings were stolen by the suspect and his alleged accomplices. Balogun Alagbado was described as a Yoruba male of average height, with an oval face, wide nose, long and wide mouth, medium lips, dark complexion and round chin. His last known address was also given as Ibadan, Oyo State. The police urged members of the public who may have information on the whereabouts of either suspect to report immediately to the nearest police station or the Office of the Commissioner of Police, SCID, Musiliu Smith Street, Panti-Yaba, Lagos State. The bulletin also provided the telephone number 08038843816 for information that could assist the police in locating the suspects. The allegations contained in the bulletin are yet to be determined by a court. The post Police declare two men wanted over alleged Ikoyi murder appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Woman pulled alive from rubble 36 hours after Colombia quake
items.description: A 32-year-old woman, who had been trapped under rubble for 36 hours following the 7.4-magnitude quake which shook western Colombia, has been rescued alive. Daniela Largo was pulled from beneath a collapsed building in the city of Pereira after a 10-hour-long rescue operation. Firefighters finally managed to reach her via a tunnel they dug below four concrete slabs under which she had been buried. At least 188 have died in the quake, according to official figures, and hundreds remain missing. In Pereira, a city in Colombia’s coffee-growing region, 79 people are confirmed to have died, the second-highest number after Cali, where 95 are dead, according to figures by the Association of Colombian Capital Cities (Asocapitales). Largo’s mother told AFP news agency that a local resident had heard her daughter cry out for help from beneath the rubble. Once emergency workers had arrived at the site, they were able to locate Largo with the help of a small camera. However, her rescue was complicated by the fact that four heavy concrete slabs were blocking the way. Local firefighters aided by colleagues deployed from the capital, Bogotá, and the disaster response team of the national police force had to dig two tunnels to reach her. Through one opening, dug from above, they were able to provide Largo with oxygen. But it was only through a second tunnel, dug from below, that they were able to free her. Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella celebrated her rescue on social media, describing it as “news which fills us with hope”. Largo’s mother said that “at home, her 12-year-old son is waiting for her”. In Pereira, at least 92 buildings collapsed. Fifteen people are known to be trapped and another 37 have been reported missing, according to Asocapitales. In Cali, Colombia’s third most populous city, more than 200 people remained trapped as of 16:00 local time on Tuesday. The city’s mayor declared a night-time curfew and said that soldiers would be on patrol in the worst-hit areas of Cali. “We need to ensure that the rescue work can be carried out safely,” he said, adding that there was still hope of finding more people alive and everyone would do their utmost to free those trapped. Eighty-seven people have been rescued in the city so far. The 7.4-magnitude quake struck at 07:34 local time (12:34 GMT) on Monday. It had its epicentre near the village of San José del Palmar, in Chocó province, but could be felt across a vast area. Seismometers nearest the epicentre registered shaking lasting between 90 seconds and two minutes. There have been more than 100 aftershocks since.

items.title: 2027: Time for Nigerians to Decide Country’s Direction — Obi
items.description: By Christopher Ameh BAUCHI — The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has called on Nigerians to take a decisive stand on the direction of the country ahead of the 2027 general elections. Obi made the call on Tuesday while delivering a goodwill remark at the 2026 Goodluck Jonathan Foundation Democracy Dialogue, held at the Ahmadu Bello International Conference Centre, Bauchi. He said Nigerians must begin to ask critical questions about the direction of the country and work collectively to reverse what he described as negative trends affecting the nation. The NDC presidential candidate stressed the need for citizens to take a definite position to ensure that the 2027 elections are conducted in a manner that strengthens democracy and produces results acceptable to all stakeholders. Speaking on the theme of the dialogue, “Beyond Elections: Can Political Parties and the Judiciary Save African Democracy?”, Obi expressed concern over what he described as the changing role of the judiciary in Nigeria’s democratic process. According to him, the judiciary previously played a significant role in strengthening democratic governance in the country. “In the past, the judiciary played positive roles in enshrining democratic leadership in Nigeria, unlike today,” he said. Obi recalled his legal battle over the Anambra State governorship, noting that some judicial officers who handled his case did so without knowing him personally. “This is a former Justice of the Supreme Court seated here. I had never met her in my life until after she wrote the judgment that made me the Governor of Anambra State. She did that without having to know me,” he said. He added that a three-member panel of the Court of Appeal had also determined his case based on its merits. “That is supposed to be the role of the judiciary in a democratic society — delivering judgment based on the merits of the facts available,” Obi said. He, however, expressed concern over what he described as political interference in the judiciary, alleging that some judicial decisions were influenced by political considerations. “What we have today is judges singing, ‘Mr President, on your mandate we shall stand.’ That is not what the judiciary is supposed to be in a true democracy,” he said. Obi therefore called on Nigerians to reflect on the direction of the country and demand responsible leadership. “Therefore, I call on the people of Nigeria. It is time for every Nigerian to sit down and find ourselves, where this nation is going. We need good leaders because there are people among us today who remain adamant and do not want a good country for our children,” he said. He commended former President Goodluck Jonathan for consistently organising the democracy dialogue, describing it as an important platform for discussions on how to strengthen democratic governance and promote judicial neutrality. Obi also urged Nigerians to reject what he described as a culture of bad governance, injustice and political manipulation, warning that decisions taken today could have consequences for future generations. He said Nigeria had the potential to become a better and more prosperous country if citizens united and demanded accountability from those entrusted with political leadership. items.title: Catholic women pledge support for efforts to combat gender-based violence
items.description: A delegation of Catholic women has pledged its support for the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection’s efforts to promote gender equality and combat gender-based violence. The delegation made the commitment when it paid a courtesy call on the Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, to discuss ways of strengthening collaboration in protecting women, children and vulnerable persons. During the engagement, the Catholic women briefed the Minister on preparations for the 2026 World Union of Catholic Women’s Organisations (WUCWO) Day Celebration and plans to launch the Coalition of Religious and Traditional Women Against Violence and Discrimination Against Women and Girls. They said the coalition would mobilise faith-based and traditional women leaders to champion the rights, safety and well-being of women and girls, particularly in communities where religious and traditional institutions wield significant influence. The delegation also highlighted the role of churches as important platforms for promoting peaceful coexistence and protecting vulnerable persons, noting that many people turn to faith-based institutions for guidance and support during difficult periods. Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey welcomed the initiative and reaffirmed the Ministry’s commitment to working with faith-based organisations to advance gender equality and strengthen efforts to prevent gender-based violence. She said collaboration with religious and traditional institutions would be important in protecting women and girls, strengthening families and promoting safer and more supportive communities.

items.title: Enugu approves N82,000 minimum wage for ESUT staff
items.description: By Alumona Ukwueze ENUGU —-The Enugu State Government has approved an increase in the minimum wage of staff of the Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT), from N32,000 to N82,000 monthly, effective September 1, 2026. The approval was contained in a letter signed by the Secretary to the Enugu State Government, Prof. Chidiebere Onyia, dated August 11, 2026, and addressed to the Accountant General of the state. According to the letter, the approval followed a report submitted by the Joint Action Committee on Trade Union (JACTU) in ESUT over issues surrounding a one-month strike ultimatum issued by the university’s unions. The government also approved an across-the-board increase of N50,000 for all other categories of staff of the university. The SSG directed the Accountant General to fully implement the approval of Governor Peter Ndubuisi Mbah. The directive referenced an earlier Government House letter dated August 7, 2026, on the matter. The letter, which was copied to the Vice-Chancellor of ESUT, Professor Aloysius-Michaels Okolie, for information and necessary action, is expected to take effect from September 1, 2026. While commenting on the matter at the 278th Regular Meeting of the Senate of the University on Wednesday, the Vice Chancellor, Professor Aloysius-Michaels Okolie, stated that the University is in further discussion with the state government for improved welfare of the staff of the University. He further stated that the South East Governors have agreed to have at least, 20% salary increase for staff of state universities in their region, adding that a governor can decide to go beyond the 20% benchmark. While thanking Governor Peter Mbah of Enugu State for the implementation of the N80,000 minimum wage and his interventions on infrastructure and academic contents in the University, he urged union leaders in the University to allow ESUT Management conclude the ongoing negotiations with the state government on the welfare of staff. The post Enugu approves N82,000 minimum wage for ESUT staff appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: AGL Guinée confirme son expertise à travers une opération logistique exceptionnelle pour la SOBRAGUI
items.description: Communiqué de presse Conakry, le 12 août 2026 Le 8 août dernier, AGL Guinée a réalisé avec succès une opération logistique d’envergure pour le compte de la SOBRAGUI, acteur industriel majeur du pays. Elle a consisté à transporter deux cuves industrielles de grande dimension du terminal à conteneurs du Port Autonome de Conakry à l’usine de la SOBRAGUI, soit une distance d’environ 6 km. Ces équipements exceptionnels, d’un diamètre de 5,2 mètres et d’une hauteur pouvant atteindre 14,3 mètres, affichent un poids unitaire de 24,6 tonnes. Leur acheminement a nécessité la mobilisation de moyens logistiques spécifiques ainsi qu’une coordination rigoureuse entre les équipes opérationnelles(…) Contact Presse : Fode Diaouné, Responsable Régional Communication & RSE Guinée – Sierra Leone – Libéria fode.diaoune@aglgroup.com – T +224 621 08 92 22 À propos d’AGL Guinée AGL Guinée est un acteur majeur des solutions logistiques et maritimes, de transport et de transit en Guinée. Depuis 2011, AGL Guinée, à travers Conakry Terminal, est l’opérateur exclusif du terminal à conteneurs du Port Autonome de Conakry avec près de 700 collaborateurs répartis entre ses filiales. Avec son agence à Kamsar, AGL Guinée accompagne le développement des projets miniers de la Guinée dans la région de Boké. AGL Guinée contribuent au développement socioéconomique de la Guinée à travers ses activités et aussi via la formation de ses collaborateurs.

items.title: Osun election: IGP Disu deploys DIG Mohammed to supervise security operations
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, has deployed Deputy Inspector-General of Police, DIG Ishyaku Mohammed, to Osun State to coordinate security operations for the governorship election scheduled for Saturday, August 15, 2026. Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Aniete Iniedu, disclosed that the deployment is part of the Nigeria Police Force’s operational strategy to ensure a peaceful, secure and credible electoral process across the state. DIG Mohammed will coordinate the police component of the election security arrangement and work closely with other security agencies under the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES). He will be supported by Assistant Inspectors-General of Police and Commissioners of Police strategically deployed across the three senatorial districts to supervise operations, strengthen intelligence-led policing and ensure prompt responses to emerging security threats. The Force said adequate security arrangements had been put in place to protect voters, INEC personnel, election materials, polling units, collation centres, accredited observers and media practitioners before, during and after the election. The IGP warned political actors, their supporters and other intending troublemakers that ballot snatching, voter intimidation, political thuggery and other electoral offences would attract immediate arrest and prosecution. Disu also reiterated the ban on armed escorts, security aides and other unauthorised persons accompanying political figures or VIPs to polling units and collation centres on election day. He further warned that state-established security outfits, quasi-security groups and private security organisations were prohibited from participating in election security duties, in line with established Nigeria Police Force election-security directives. The Nigeria Police Force reassured residents, voters and visitors to Osun State of adequate security, urging eligible citizens to exercise their civic rights peacefully and without fear. The Force reaffirmed its commitment to professionalism, neutrality, respect for human rights and the protection of the integrity of the electoral process. items.title: Gunmen kill two, injure one, burn houses in Plateau attacks
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — Two persons have been killed while another sustained injuries in fresh attacks on Berom communities in Plateau State, the Berom Youth Moulders-Association (BYM) has said. The attacks occurred on Tuesday night in at least four locations, including Gwa-Wereng Rim, Kyeng Village in Bachi District, Dorong and Jol Village. A resident of the affected area, Lyop Gabriel, said the attack on Gwa-Wereng Rim occurred at about 9:30 p.m. when gunmen reportedly invaded the community and opened fire on residents. In a statement issued on Wednesday, the National Publicity Secretary of BYM, Rwang Tengwong, said the attackers killed Bulus Mwagwong, popularly known as Dikko, at Gwa-Wereng Rim, while his cousin, Yakubu, sustained serious injuries. The association said 47-year-old Stephen Dachollom Kaze was also killed by suspected attackers at Kyeng Village, Bachi District, at about 8:30 p.m. According to the statement, another attack occurred in Dorong, where the attackers allegedly set houses ablaze, destroying property and forcing residents to flee. At Jol Village, armed attackers reportedly engaged local vigilantes in a gun battle, further heightening tension in the community. Reacting to the incidents, BYM, under the leadership of its President, Dalyop Solomon Mwantiri, condemned the attacks, describing them as a disturbing threat to the lives, livelihoods and safety of rural communities. The association expressed concern over the alleged increasing frequency of attacks on communities, particularly farmers and other residents who depend on their farmlands for their livelihoods. BYM called on security agencies to strengthen their presence in vulnerable communities, intensify surveillance and apprehend those responsible for the attacks. It also urged the authorities to ensure that perpetrators of the killings and destruction were arrested and prosecuted. The association appealed to the Plateau State Government and other relevant authorities to provide immediate assistance to affected families and communities, particularly those who lost loved ones, homes and other property in the attacks. BYM condoled with the families of Mwagwong and Kaze and wished Yakubu a speedy recovery. The association also urged residents to remain vigilant, peaceful and united, stressing the need for concerted efforts to prevent further escalation of violence in the affected communities. It called for urgent and decisive security action to protect lives and property and restore confidence among residents. The post Gunmen kill two, injure one, burn houses in Plateau attacks appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ayra Starr’s mother promotes ‘Starr Girl’ album on Lagos streets
items.description: The mother of Afrobeats star, Oyinkansola Aderibigbe, popularly known as Ayra Starr, Nene Aderibigbe, has promoted her daughter’s forthcoming ”Starr Girl” album on the streets of Lagos ahead of its Friday release. Aderibigbe, popularly known as Genzmummy on Instagram, shared a video showing herself, the singer’s sister and other women promoting the album. The caption reads: “We declare starrgirl album to God in the name of the father and the son and of the holy ghost” The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the women were dressed in matching black outfits and purple headgear while holding placards promoting ”Starr Girl”. The placards carried messages including “Stargirl album out on the 14th of August” as the women promoted the forthcoming project on the streets. The street campaign comes as Ayra Starr prepares to release ”Starr Girl”, her third studio album, following 19 & Dangerous, and The Year I Turned 21. Aderibigbe, was born in Cotonou, Benin Republic, and raised in Lagos, Nigeria. She rose to prominence after signing with Mavin Records and releasing her self-titled debut EP in 2021. She subsequently released 19 & Dangerous in 2021, followed by The Year I Turned 21 in May 2024. Her 2022 single “Rush” earned a nomination for Best African Music Performance at the 66th Grammy Awards. Ayra Starr had earlier announced that ”Starr Girl” would be released on Aug. 14, with the project expected to mark her latest album release. (NAN) The post Ayra Starr’s mother promotes ‘Starr Girl’ album on Lagos streets appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Médusée : la plus grande centrale nucléaire française presque en arrêt à cause des méduses
items.description: Un afflux massif de meduses a de nouveau perturbe le fonctionnement de la centrale nucleaire de Gravelines, la plus importante de France. Trois de ses six reacteurs ont ete arretes, tandis qu'un quatrieme fonctionne desormais a puissance reduite. Plus concretement, les reacteurs 3 et 4 se sont mis automatiquement a l'arret conformement aux procedures d'exploitation. Le personnel de la centrale a ensuite decide d'arreter le reacteur 2 et de reduire de moitie la puissance du reacteur 1. Le reacteur 5 etant deja immobilise pour une operation de maintenance programmee, seul le reacteur 6 continue actuellement de fonctionner normalement. De son cote, electricite de France (EDF) a assure que l'incident n'avait eu aucune consequence sur la sûrete des installations, sur le personnel de la centrale ou sur l'environnement. Ce n'est pas la premiere fois que les meduses perturbent l'activite du site. En août 2025, leur presence avait obstrue les systemes de refroidissement de la centrale et provoque l'arret automatique de quatre reacteurs. a la suite de cet episode, EDF avait renforce son dispositif de surveillance afin de detecter plus rapidement de nouveaux afflux et d'en limiter les consequences. Des cameras fixes ont notamment ete installees au niveau des canaux d'arrivee d'eau et des tambours filtrants pour reperer au plus tot d'eventuelles obstructions. Dans le meme temps, l'energeticien travaille egalement avec une organisation francaise de pecheurs et une organisation de sauvetage en mer chargee de surveiller l'apparition d'importants groupes de meduses. En cas d'alerte, des operations de chalutage ciblees peuvent etre lancees afin de reduire leur concentration avant qu'elles n'atteignent la centrale. Les meduses ne sont d'ailleurs pas le seul probleme auquel le nucleaire francais doit faire face. La chaleur et la secheresse ont egalement contraint les centrales a reduire leur production. Le 9 août, 15,6 % de la puissance du parc nucleaire francais etait indisponible pour ces raisons, soit la proportion la plus elevee enregistree depuis qu'EDF publie ces donnees, en 2015. Cette baisse s'explique par les besoins importants en eau des centrales nucleaires pour refroidir leurs installations. Lorsque les rivieres se rechauffent ou que leur niveau baisse, certains reacteurs doivent reduire leur puissance.

items.title: Accord avec le FMI : la Guinée mise sur 425 millions de dollars pour accélérer ses réformes économiques
items.description: À la suite de la conclusion d’un accord avec le Fonds monétaire international (FMI) en vue d’un nouveau programme économique et financier appuyé par la Facilité élargie de crédit (FEC), le pool économique du gouvernement a animé, mardi 11 août 2026, un point de presse pour en expliquer les contours. Le programme, prévu sur 41 mois, devrait permettre à la Guinée d’accéder à environ 425 millions de dollars américains, sous réserve de l’approbation du Conseil d’administration du FMI. Face aux journalistes, la ministre de l’Économie, des Finances et du Budget, Mariama Ciré Sylla, le ministre du Plan, de la Coopération internationale et du Développement, Ismaël Nabé, et le gouverneur de la Banque centrale de la République de Guinée (BCRG), Dr Karamo Kaba, ont présenté cet accord comme un instrument destiné à accompagner les réformes économiques et la transformation structurelle du pays. Mariama Ciré Sylla : « Le programme est d’abord le programme de la Guinée » Dans son intervention, Mariama Ciré Sylla a présenté l’accord comme « une étape importante dans la trajectoire économique » de la Guinée. Selon elle, il intervient à un moment où les autorités entendent consolider les équilibres macroéconomiques tout en renforçant la mobilisation des ressources internes et la gestion des finances publiques. La ministre a notamment mis en exergue les performances économiques enregistrées ces dernières années. Selon les chiffres qu’elle a communiqués, la croissance s’est établie à 6,9% en 2025 et devrait atteindre 8,6% en 2026. Les recettes fiscales seraient, quant à elles, passées de 8,6% du PIB en 2024 à 11,3% en 2025. « La Guinée n’aborde pas ce nouveau programme avec le FMI en situation de crise ou de faiblesse, mais plutôt avec des acquis, avec des ambitions, avec des ressources considérables et avec la volonté de durablement changer d’échelle », a-t-elle déclaré. Pour Mariama Ciré Sylla, l’enjeu est désormais de faire en sorte que la croissance, notamment celle portée par l’expansion du secteur minier et les investissements dans les infrastructures, se traduise par une amélioration durable des conditions de vie. Le programme s’articule ainsi autour de cinq priorités : la mobilisation durable des recettes publiques, la gestion rigoureuse des finances publiques, la stabilité macroéconomique et financière, la gouvernance et la transparence, ainsi que la diversification économique et la promotion du capital humain. Sur le plan budgétaire, les autorités entendent notamment élargir l’assiette fiscale, lutter contre la fraude, poursuivre la digitalisation des régies financières, améliorer la préparation du budget et renforcer la sélection des investissements publics. « Nous réformons parce que la Guinée en a besoin. Nous réformons parce que nous voulons mobiliser davantage de recettes pour financer nous-mêmes nos écoles, nos hôpitaux, nos routes, l’accès à l’eau et à l’électricité et nos infrastructures », a expliqué la ministre. Elle estime ainsi que le FMI vient accompagner une stratégie définie par les autorités guinéennes, et non s’y substituer. « Une économie performante n’a de sens que si elle permet à nos populations de mieux vivre. La croissance dont on parle doit devenir des emplois. Nos recettes minières doivent devenir des routes, des écoles, des hôpitaux et de l’électricité », a-t-elle insisté. Ismaël Nabé : « Bien davantage qu’un accord financier » Pour le ministre du Plan, de la Coopération internationale et du Développement, Ismaël Nabé, les discussions avec le FMI vont au-delà du financement attendu. « C’est un signal de crédibilité, c’est un signal de confiance, mais surtout un signal de responsabilité », a-t-il déclaré. Selon lui, la stabilité macroéconomique recherchée dans le cadre du programme ne constitue pas une finalité, mais doit servir de fondement à la transformation économique. « Nous ne stabilisons pas l’économie pour stabiliser l’économie, nous stabilisons notre économie pour pouvoir investir davantage dans nos routes, dans nos énergies, dans notre agriculture, dans nos industries, dans nos systèmes éducatifs, dans la santé, mais surtout dans le capital humain », a expliqué Ismaël Nabé. Le ministre a également insisté sur la nécessité de préserver la maîtrise nationale des politiques économiques. « Le partenariat, ce n’est pas une relation de dépendance », a-t-il souligné, estimant que les réformes doivent être appropriées par les institutions guinéennes, adaptées aux réalités du pays et cohérentes avec ses ambitions de long terme. Dans le cadre du programme, son département entend concentrer son action sur trois chantiers : le renforcement de la planification stratégique et de son articulation avec le budget et l’investissement public ; la modernisation du système statistique national ; et l’alignement de la coopération internationale sur les priorités nationales. Pour Ismaël Nabé, les 425 millions de dollars attendus doivent également contribuer à renforcer la crédibilité de la Guinée et faciliter la mobilisation d’autres financements auprès des partenaires bilatéraux et multilatéraux ainsi que des investisseurs. « Les indicateurs macroéconomiques n’ont de sens que lorsqu’ils améliorent la vie de la population », a-t-il insisté. Karamo Kaba : « Nous devons passer d’une culture de l’annonce à une culture de la réalisation » Le gouverneur de la Banque centrale de la République de Guinée, Dr Karamo Kaba, a, pour sa part, placé son intervention sous le signe de la stabilité, de la responsabilité et de la transformation économique. « Cet accord n’est pas simplement un accord financier. Il constitue un contrat de conscience autour d’une vision, celle d’une Guinée capable de tirer pleinement parti de ses ressources, de préserver ses équilibres économiques et de préparer une prospérité durable », a-t-il déclaré. Sous réserve de l’approbation du Conseil d’administration du FMI, attendue selon lui en septembre, la Guinée devrait avoir accès à environ 425 millions de dollars, représentant 145% de sa quote-part au FMI. Mais pour le gouverneur de la BCRG, la portée du programme dépasse le montant du financement. « Sa véritable valeur réside dans la crédibilité qu’il apporte à notre politique économique, dans l’ancrage qu’il donne à nos réformes et dans la confiance qu’il peut susciter auprès des investisseurs et de nos partenaires », a-t-il soutenu. Karamo Kaba a également évoqué les perspectives de croissance de l’économie guinéenne. Après une progression estimée à 6,9% en 2025, il table sur une croissance d’environ 8,8% en 2026 et avoisinant 10% entre 2027 et 2030, notamment sous l’effet de la montée en puissance du secteur minier et de Simandou. À ses yeux, le mégaprojet minier doit toutefois dépasser la seule augmentation des exportations de minerai. « Simandou représente bien davantage qu’un projet minier. Il doit être un accélérateur de la transformation économique. Notre ambition n’est pas simplement d’exporter davantage de minerai, elle est de faire en sorte que la richesse créée par nos ressources naturelles contribue à développer nos infrastructures, créer des emplois, renforcer notre secteur privé et faire émerger de nouvelles chaînes de valeur en Guinée », a-t-il expliqué. Pour le gouverneur, c’est à cette capacité de transformer les ressources naturelles en développement que doit se mesurer la souveraineté économique du pays. Il a, dans la foulée, interpellé sur la nécessité de rendre la croissance perceptible dans le quotidien des citoyens : « À quoi sert une croissance de 8% si elle ne se traduit pas par davantage d’emplois, de meilleures infrastructures, plus d’électricité, plus d’agriculture, de meilleures écoles et davantage d’opportunités pour notre jeunesse ? » « La croissance doit changer la vie de tous les jours », a-t-il poursuivi, estimant qu’elle doit permettre au citoyen d’accéder à l’emploi, à l’entrepreneur de développer son activité, à l’agriculteur d’accroître sa production et au pays de transformer davantage ses matières premières localement. Cinq priorités pour la Banque centrale Dans cette perspective, Dr Karamo Kaba a décliné cinq priorités autour desquelles devrait s’articuler l’action des autorités. La première consiste à mobiliser davantage de recettes publiques, notamment celles provenant du secteur minier, tout en renforçant la transparence et la bonne gouvernance. La deuxième vise à améliorer la qualité de la dépense publique. La troisième porte sur la préservation de la stabilité macroéconomique et financière. À ce niveau, le gouverneur insiste particulièrement sur la stabilité monétaire, le renforcement des réserves de change et la solidité du système financier, qu’il considère comme des conditions indispensables à la souveraineté économique. La quatrième priorité concerne le renforcement de la gouvernance et des institutions économiques, à travers davantage de transparence, de redevabilité et une amélioration de la qualité des politiques publiques. Enfin, la cinquième porte sur la diversification de l’économie guinéenne afin de réduire sa vulnérabilité et sa dépendance à certains secteurs. « Être souverain ne signifie pas s’isoler. Être souverain, c’est être capable de choisir, c’est disposer d’institutions solides, maîtriser ses finances publiques, préserver ses réserves, attirer les investissements dans de bonnes conditions et surtout être capable de transformer ses propres ressources en développement », a expliqué Karamo Kaba. Selon lui, la Guinée doit donc continuer à travailler avec ses partenaires, mais avec des institutions renforcées, une économie plus diversifiée et une capacité accrue à décider de son avenir. Faire de Simandou un « catalyseur » du développement Revenant sur Simandou, le gouverneur de la BCRG estime que la Guinée dispose d’une « opportunité exceptionnelle », dont la réussite dépendra cependant de la vision, de la discipline et de la bonne gouvernance. « Nous devons faire de Simandou un véritable catalyseur de développement national. Les infrastructures doivent bénéficier à l’économie dans son ensemble. Les investissements doivent stimuler les entreprises guinéennes. Les emplois et les compétences doivent bénéficier à notre jeunesse », a-t-il affirmé. L’objectif, selon lui, est de transformer la richesse naturelle en capital économique, humain et institutionnel. Mais le gouverneur a surtout insisté sur la phase qui s’ouvre après la conclusion de l’accord technique. Pour lui, l’enjeu sera désormais moins celui des annonces que celui de l’exécution des engagements pris. « Nous devons passer d’une culture de l’annonce à une culture de la réalisation. Annoncer moins, faire davantage, mesurer les résultats, corriger ce qui doit l’être et rendre compte aux citoyens. Le véritable travail commence maintenant », a-t-il lancé. Il poursuit : « Nous devons transformer les engagements en réformes, les réformes en investissements, les investissements en emploi et la croissance en progrès concret pour chaque Guinéen. » Karamo Kaba estime ainsi que la Guinée doit désormais franchir une nouvelle étape dans l’exploitation de son potentiel économique : « La Guinée n’est plus simplement un pays qui regarde son potentiel. Elle doit désormais transformer ce potentiel en puissance économique. » Le gouverneur a conclu en affichant l’ambition d’aboutir à « une Guinée stable, une Guinée prospère, une Guinée souveraine, une Guinée qui crée des emplois, transforme ses ressources et prépare l’avenir ».

Sur une prevision budgetaire de plus de 95 millions de francs CFA, la mairie dit avoir mobilise plus de 77 millions , soit un taux de realisation de 79 % . A Koulikoro, c'est sur le defi de l'acces a l'eau que la Journee a ete magnifiee. Plus de 50 % des habitants de la region seraient confrontes a des besoins en eau, selon les informations donnees durant la rencontre. Une conference-debat et des visites de terrain ont permis de mettre en lumiere les defis lies a l'eau, a l'assainissement et au developpement local. items.title: Fulham prépare une nouvelle offre pour Abdelhamid Ait Boudlal
items.description: Fulham ne renonce pas à Abdelhamid Ait Boudlal. Après une première proposition refusée par le Stade Rennais, le club anglais s’apprêterait à revenir à la charge pour tenter de convaincre le club breton de laisser partir le jeune défenseur marocain. Le dossier Abdelhamid Ait Boudlal pourrait connaître un nouveau rebondissement. Selon Foot Mercato, Fulham prépare une nouvelle offre pour le défenseur marocain de 20 ans, après avoir déjà essuyé un premier refus du Stade Rennais. Le club anglais souhaite renforcer son secteur défensif et aurait ciblé le jeune Marocain, qui s’est progressivement imposé dans l’effectif rennais. Le Stade Rennais ne semble toutefois pas disposé à se séparer facilement de son jeune défenseur. Abdelhamid Ait Boudlal a disputé 21 rencontres toutes compétitions confondues la saison dernière, ce qui témoigne de l’importance qu’il a prise au sein de l’équipe. Le club français compte ainsi conserver son joueur et ne souhaite pas, pour le moment, donner suite aux sollicitations de Fulham. De son côté, le défenseur marocain serait favorable à une expérience en Premier League. Son ouverture à un départ vers l’Angleterre pourrait donc encourager Fulham à intensifier ses démarches dans les prochains jours. Formé à l’Académie Mohammed VI de football, Abdelhamid Ait Boudlal est considéré comme l’un des jeunes défenseurs marocains les plus prometteurs. Il avait notamment été retenu parmi les candidats au Golden Boy, une distinction qui récompense les meilleurs jeunes joueurs évoluant en Europe. Fulham devrait donc revenir à la charge avec une nouvelle proposition. Reste à savoir si cette deuxième offre sera suffisamment convaincante pour faire évoluer la position du Stade Rennais et permettre à Abdelhamid Ait Boudlal de découvrir la Premier League. items.title: Ebonyi Assembly passes bill regulating scrap trade, rents, agent fees
items.description: Ebonyi House of Assembly has passed into law a bill regulating scrap trade, house rents and estate agent fees to curb exploitation and vandalism. The legislation, passed during plenary presided over by the Speaker, Mr Moses Odunwa, is titled ”The Ebonyi State Sale of Scraps, House Rent and Agent Fees Regulation Law, 2026”. The law, deemed to commence immediately if assented to by Gov. Francis Nwifuru, sought to regulate the sale, possession, transportation and disposal of metal and electrical scraps, standardise house rents and curb excessive agent fees. It prohibits the purchase, sale, possession for sale, transportation or disposal of metal or electrical scraps except by licensed dealers operating in accordance with regulations made under the law. The legislation proposes imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years or a fine of up to N500,000 to offenders. The legislation also stipulates that landlords who obtain possession of accommodation through fraud, misrepresentation or concealment of material facts commit an offence punishable by up to two years’ imprisonment. It further limits agents’ fees to not more than two per cent of the gross sum of a property transaction. From the commencement of the law, landlords are required to comply with standard rents prescribed by the governor for applicable categories of accommodation. The law also requires all estate agents operating in the state capital to register with the Ministry of Capital City to promote transparency and professionalism in property transactions. Presenting the bill, the House Leader, Kingsley Ikoro, said the legislation was designed to check vandalism, environmental degradation and exploitative practices in the housing sector. “This legislation is very important to us as a people because it will help check vandalism of critical assets, environmental degradation and exploitative practices in the housing sector,” Ikoro said. Contributing to the debate, Victor Nwoke, Aloysius Nwodo, Oluchukwu Ezeali, Friday Ogbuewu and Celestine Ogba described the legislation as timely and necessary to address scrap theft and arbitrary rent increases. The speaker noted that scrap dealers had caused considerable havoc in society, adding that if acted on, the legislation would promote public safety and restore sanity to property transactions. The bill was considered clause by clause by the Committee of the Whole, with members correcting identified grammatical errors before unanimously passing it into law. The House also adopted the state Auditor-General’s report on the consolidated financial statements of the Ebonyi Government for the year ended Dec. 31, 2025, which it said conformed with accepted accounting principles. The lawmakers screened and confirmed nine nominees of the governor as coordinator and members of the management committee of Amasiri Development Centre, Afikpo Local Government Area. The screening follows the reinstatement of the development centre, which had earlier been disbanded and delisted by the Ebonyi Government. items.title: Demande de pétrole: L'Agence internationale de l'énergie revoit ses prévisions à la baisse
items.description: L'Agence internationale de l'énergie (AIE) a indiqué mercredi revoir en baisse sa prévision de la demande mondiale de pétrole en 2026, dans le sillage du conflit au Moyen-Orient et de la flambée des prix des hydrocarbures. L'Agence de l'énergie de l'OCDE table désormais sur une baisse de 1,6 million de barils par jour (mb/j) sur un an, alors qu'elle anticipait un recul de 1 mb/j dans sa précédente estimation en juillet. La consommation mondiale pétrolière s'établirait en 2026 à 103,29 mb/j, contre 103,46 mb/j estimée le mois dernier. « La fermeture prolongée du détroit d’Ormuz et la hausse des prix des carburants continuent de peser sur la consommation de pétrole », a souligné l'AIE dans son rapport qui révise chaque mois ses prévisions sur les marchés pétroliers en fonction de la conjoncture. L'AIE envisage toutefois une amélioration progressive: après une contraction de 4,9 mb/j au 2e trimestre et de 2,8 mb/j au 3e trimestre, elle devrait retrouver une croissance de 0,58 mb/j au tout dernier trimestre. L'offre mondiale reste elle toujours pénalisée par la fermeture persistante du détroit d’Ormuz qui perturbe les chaînes d’approvisionnement internationales et réduisent la disponibilité des produits pétroliers. Environ 8,3 millions de barils par jour de la production du Golfe sont ainsi toujours manquants en raison de la crise d'Ormuz, qualifiée par l'AIE de « plus grande perturbation de l’offre mondiale de pétrole jamais enregistrée ». En conséquence, la pénurie de produits raffinés, notamment aggravée par les attaques ukrainiennes contre les raffineries russes, a propulsé les marges de raffinage dans le bassin Atlantique à des « niveaux record en juillet », « le diesel atteignant une valeur deux fois supérieure à celle du brut sur les marchés internationaux ». La production mondiale de pétrole devrait désormais reculer en moyenne de 4,3 mb/j en 2026, à 102,02 mb/j et rebondir de 8,3 mb/j l’an prochain pour atteindre 110,3 mb/j. Selon l'AIE, une « désescalade » dans le conflit, devrait permettre « une reprise progressive des flux dans les mois à venir » et laisser entrevoir la possibilité d'un surplus d'offre pétrolière vers le 4e trimestre 2026, qui permettrait par la suite de reconstituer les stocks de pétrole. Des perspectives d'amélioration qui restent néanmoins « fragiles ». « Même si le marché devrait renouer avec un excédent vers la fin de cette année, les risques restent importants et l'urgence de rouvrir le détroit s'est accrue, les réserves de sécurité dont on disposait auparavant s'épuisant rapidement », a mis en garde l'AIE.
